bearer: Consequential software structures and decisions, at a declared scope rather than a fixed diagram granularity.
criterion: Identify decisions whose cross-cutting consequences, dependency reach, qualities or change costs justify architectural treatment; state why each is significant rather than relying on job title or diagram level.
name: Consequence-bound architectural significance
non_trigger: Handle genuinely local, reversible choices within ordinary design and code review; do not create an architectural record for every edit.
trigger: A decision can change a stakeholder outcome beyond its local implementation or would be costly to reverse.

bearer: Stakeholder concerns related to system-wide and boundary-level choices.
criterion: Connect each material concern to an architectural question, a scenario or constraint and the decision that consumes it; expose conflicts and missing participation.
name: Stakeholder concerns connected to decisions
non_trigger: For a small shared-understanding team, discuss the few consequential concerns directly and retain only what later action needs.
trigger: Different users, maintainers, operators or sponsors bear materially different consequences.

bearer: Intended architecture, architecture description and realised software/configuration as separate referents.
criterion: Keep intended structure, its representation and claims about the actual system distinguishable; attach a basis and observation scope to assertions of correspondence.
name: Architecture, description and belief distinguished
non_trigger: Inspect the relevant code/configuration/execution directly when the system is small; a separate comprehensive model is unnecessary.
trigger: A decision depends on a diagram, repository model, recovered graph or architect’s account being true of the real system.

bearer: System concepts and cross-component behavioural commitments.
criterion: Keep the user-visible and developer-facing concepts and essential invariants coherent across decisions, while allowing local variation that does not damage them.
name: Conceptual integrity without mandatory centralisation
non_trigger: Use shared examples and a small vocabulary in one team; do not impose a chief architect or one technology solely to look unified.
trigger: Independent decisions would expose incompatible meanings or behaviours to common consumers.

bearer: Consequential decisions and commitments at organisational/software interfaces.
criterion: Make it clear who can accept a consequential trade-off, who must be consulted and who can execute it; neither identifying a concern nor holding a meeting grants permission to act.
name: Accountable authority for consequential trade-offs
non_trigger: Existing role agreements and a direct decision conversation may suffice; do not invent a new approval body.
trigger: A change alters commitments or transfers risk/cost across roles, teams or external parties.

bearer: Definitional boundary between architecture and other consequential work.
criterion: Candidate shorthand groups salient decisions, but without a scope or consequence test it does not determine what architectural work should occur.
name: Architecture as an unrestricted important-decisions label
non_trigger: Use the consequence-bound criterion in ESA-001 and state the architectural object.
trigger: The label is used to claim authority over all important engineering or business matters.

bearer: Module responsibilities and design-knowledge boundaries, not deployment units.
criterion: Place knowledge of a plausibly varying design decision behind an interface whose clients need not depend on that decision; separate stable obligations from hidden choices.
name: Change-oriented information hiding
non_trigger: Keep a straightforward local implementation where the variation is unlikely or the extra boundary costs more than the expected change.
trigger: A likely change currently propagates through clients that need only the stable service or invariant.

bearer: Semantic contracts at component, service or connector boundaries.
criterion: Express consequential assumptions about state, control, ordering, data meaning, faults and side effects at the interface; check the assumptions actually relied on by both sides.
name: Semantic interface assumptions made testable
non_trigger: Use concrete examples, assertions or focused integration tests for a narrow local interface; a full formal contract is not mandatory.
trigger: Parts are composed, reused or replaced and nominal signatures do not capture their operating expectations.

bearer: Runtime and logical interaction relations, at the level required by the concern.
criterion: Model or inspect the actual interaction mechanism—call, event, stream, shared store or protocol—and its control/data consequences instead of treating an arrow as self-explanatory.
name: Connectors as explicit interaction mechanisms
non_trigger: Name and test a simple direct call; do not create a connector abstraction or framework when ordinary language captures the needed semantics.
trigger: Interaction semantics affect coupling, performance, consistency, failure handling or allowed composition.

bearer: Typed relationships between software responsibilities, runtime units and work items.
criterion: Distinguish compile/import, invocation, data, correctness, deployment and change dependencies; choose the relation that can answer the architectural question.
name: Dependency kinds and uses relations distinguished
non_trigger: Inspect the few relevant dependencies manually; do not build a global graph when a local semantic explanation suffices.
trigger: A dependency graph is being used to infer independence, change impact or coordination needs.

bearer: Fault, state and change-containment boundaries across components or deployments.
criterion: Demonstrate the claimed containment property under the relevant fault or change, including shared state, resources and management channels; distinguish naming a boundary from enforcing it.
name: Demonstrated containment rather than nominal isolation
non_trigger: Do not claim independence where it is unnecessary; a coordinated shared unit can be the simpler honest design.
trigger: A design relies on independent failure, deployment, access or change behaviour.

bearer: Logical, team and deployment boundary choices, which need not coincide.
criterion: Place boundaries by considering change coupling, communication, translation and operation costs together; compare local and distributed alternatives.
name: Coordination-aware boundary placement
non_trigger: Keep collaborating responsibilities in a coherent local module/deployment when independent operation has no demonstrated consumer.
trigger: A boundary can reduce change propagation but creates a material coordination or runtime burden.

bearer: Architecture of related program families, shared assets and variation boundaries.
criterion: Identify common and varying obligations across a genuine set of related systems, then arrange abstractions and uses relations to support required variants or subsets.
name: Commonality and variability within an architectural family
non_trigger: Build the single required system directly when a family is speculative; defer variation points with no credible consumer.
trigger: Multiple related products or configurations have known shared structure and deliberate variation.

bearer: Quality requirements at the system or affected architectural element.
criterion: Express a quality concern through stimulus, source, environment, affected artefact, response and response measure, tailoring detail to the decision being made.
name: Measurable quality-attribute scenarios
non_trigger: A short, concrete example with an observable acceptable response can suffice; do not fill six empty boxes ceremonially.
trigger: A quality term such as fast, secure, usable or modifiable must discriminate between designs.

bearer: Scenario population, sampling and prioritisation at evaluation scope.
criterion: Examine which users, operating states, changes and adverse cases the scenario set represents; add decision-changing omissions and preserve uncertainty rather than treating prioritisation as completeness.
name: Scenario population and selection validity
non_trigger: Use a few explicit favourable, adverse and boundary cases for a small decision, with limits stated; avoid exhaustive catalogues with no consumer.
trigger: An evaluation or design claim depends on a selected set of scenarios.

bearer: Architectural tactic acting on performance, availability, security, modifiability or other modelled qualities.
criterion: Connect a tactic to the model parameters it changes and to the response sought; account for interactions, overhead and assumptions that make the causal explanation plausible.
name: Tactics tied to explanatory quality models
non_trigger: Use a targeted prototype or direct simplification instead of a tactic taxonomy when it answers the causal question more cheaply.
trigger: A structural or behavioural intervention is proposed to improve a quality attribute.

bearer: Multi-quality architectural alternatives and external constraints.
criterion: Separate hard constraints from preferences, compare effects on multiple concerns and make the chosen sacrifice explicit; do not aggregate away unacceptable consequences.
name: Explicit interacting-quality trade-offs and constraints
non_trigger: Eliminate dominated or infeasible options through a brief explicit comparison when elaborate utility modelling adds no decision value.
trigger: Improving one response can worsen another or transfer cost to a different stakeholder.

bearer: Empirical evidence about realised architectural behaviour, not just models.
criterion: Validate important predictions against observations whose workload, faults, configuration and measurement boundary are representative of the decision; distinguish the measurement from the whole quality claim.
name: Representative workload and failure observations
non_trigger: Use the smallest representative experiment or inspect existing evidence; do not run a broad benchmark suite unrelated to the risk.
trigger: A prototype, benchmark, trace or field observation is being used to accept an architecture.

bearer: An inadmissible general optimisation claim over architectural qualities.
criterion: Independent maximisation ignores interaction and feasibility; it is not retained as an engineering rule.
name: Independent maximisation of every quality
non_trigger: Use ESA-017 to compare constrained alternatives and identify any genuine dominated option.
trigger: A proposal claims every quality improves without defining resource, stakeholder or environmental boundaries.

bearer: Architecture descriptions and viewpoint conventions at concern-specific abstraction levels.
criterion: Select viewpoints by the concerns and decisions they enable, then create only the views needed to communicate or analyse those concerns.
name: Concern-selected views and viewpoints
non_trigger: A single annotated sketch or direct walkthrough may suffice when it answers every consequential question at hand.
trigger: One representation obscures materially different structural, runtime, deployment or development questions.

bearer: Cross-view and description–implementation relations, not visual layout similarity.
criterion: Identify how entities and relations in different views correspond, then check consequential consistency and the link to implementation/configuration/operation.
name: Correspondence between views and realisation
non_trigger: Check a small set of named correspondences manually rather than maintain a universal metamodel.
trigger: A decision combines claims from several views or uses a model as evidence about implementation.

bearer: Formal component/connector/configuration or behaviour models.
criterion: Use a formal description when a consequential property can be expressed and analysed under a tractable model; keep the guarantee, assumptions and implementation mapping explicit.
name: Formal architectural descriptions with bounded guarantees
non_trigger: A focused protocol model, contract or ordinary test can dominate a whole-system ADL when it answers the risk.
trigger: An interaction/configuration property justifies stronger analysis than informal review or testing alone.

bearer: An unconditional documentation ritual rather than a system property.
criterion: Completing a prescribed view set regardless of its consumers is ceremony, not a generally useful mechanism.
name: Mandatory complete 4+1 documentation
non_trigger: Select views through ESA-020; omit views that add no needed distinction or communication.
trigger: A review treats the existence of all five views as evidence of architectural adequacy.

bearer: Inferred architectural structures and behaviours from realised artefacts.
criterion: Combine appropriate static, configuration, dynamic and human evidence to reconstruct only the architectural facts needed; label extraction scope, ambiguity and unobserved behaviour.
name: Triangulated architecture reconstruction with uncertainty
non_trigger: Inspect the relevant implementation paths with an experienced maintainer before building an automated whole-system reconstruction.
trigger: Reliable architectural knowledge is missing or an existing description is suspect.

bearer: Component-and-connector styles and recurring architectural solution structures.
criterion: Use a style or pattern as a conditional mechanism with an explicit problem, constraints and trade-offs; document purposeful hybrids and their interaction obligations.
name: Styles and patterns as conditional mechanisms
non_trigger: Use a direct design without a pattern label when the pattern adds indirection or excludes a better local arrangement.
trigger: A recurring architectural problem matches the style’s assumptions closely enough to reduce design or analysis effort.

bearer: Architectural alternatives and decision counterfactuals.
criterion: Compare feasible architectural options, including retaining the present design or a smaller intervention, against the same concerns and assumptions; expose excluded options.
name: Comparison with feasible alternatives and no change
non_trigger: Use a short explicit comparison when one option is plainly dominated; do not fabricate many alternatives for a form.
trigger: A consequential investment or restructuring is being justified.

bearer: Architecture under prospective functional or quality-related modifications.
criterion: Walk representative modifications through an architecture, identify affected elements and interacting scenarios, and compare the resulting burdens across alternatives.
name: Change-scenario architectural evaluation
non_trigger: Walk a single realistic change through the current code and a proposed alternative if a full workshop is unnecessary.
trigger: Modifiability or the consequences of planned change are material and can be expressed as concrete scenarios.

bearer: Multi-quality evaluation of an architectural candidate.
criterion: Bring business/mission drivers, architecture and quality scenarios into a structured review to identify assumptions, risks, sensitivity points and trade-offs that need a decision.
name: Multi-quality risk and sensitivity evaluation
non_trigger: Use a focused risk/assumption review with the necessary participants for a small decision; the full event structure is not mandatory.
trigger: Several consequential qualities interact and missing assumptions justify a facilitated multi-stakeholder review.

bearer: Architectural investment alternatives, costs and stakeholder preference models.
criterion: Establish feasible options and hard constraints first, then explore plausible costs, utilities, dependencies and sensitivity rather than treating one estimated ratio as an objective answer.
name: Economic evaluation with uncertainty and dependency
non_trigger: Use cost ranges, break-even reasoning or dominance checks when a detailed utility model adds unjustified precision.
trigger: Several acceptable alternatives compete for constrained resources and economic consequences may change the choice.

bearer: Prototype, simulation or analytic model tied to a real architectural decision.
criterion: Choose a focused prototype, simulation or analytic model for the uncertainty at hand; calibrate it where possible and distinguish omitted behaviour from demonstrated behaviour.
name: Targeted prototypes and calibrated analytic models
non_trigger: Use a small experiment or direct inspection of the uncertain mechanism rather than a production-like prototype of everything.
trigger: A consequential prediction cannot be judged adequately by reasoning or existing observations alone.

bearer: Inference from evaluation process completion to realised performance or correctness.
criterion: A review can establish that a process occurred and risks were considered; it cannot by itself guarantee the real system under unexamined conditions.
name: Review success as a guarantee of operating quality
non_trigger: Keep the review’s actual conclusions and obtain the missing representative evidence through ESA-018.
trigger: An approval, risk list or completed workshop is used as conclusive evidence that the system will meet its qualities.

bearer: Architectural decision knowledge linked to structures, constraints and evidence.
criterion: Preserve the context, selected option, significant alternatives, consequences and assumptions that a future actor needs to understand or revise a consequential decision.
name: Recoverable decision rationale for later consumers
non_trigger: A short linked note or direct shared understanding can suffice for a local reversible decision; do not record all reasoning exhaustively.
trigger: A decision is non-obvious, likely to recur or needs to survive turnover and distributed work.

bearer: Time-indexed architectural decisions and their dependency links.
criterion: Keep a decision’s status and reopening conditions visible; distinguish superseding it from erasing the evidence that once justified it.
name: Decision ageing, supersession and reopening
non_trigger: Update a short status/link at the affected decision; no periodic meeting is needed when nothing decision-relevant has changed.
trigger: Architectural choices outlive their original workload, team, dependency or business assumptions.

bearer: Coupling between software/work dependencies and human communication.
criterion: Identify consequential technical/work dependencies and arrange adequate communication across the people who must coordinate them; test the actual coordination problem rather than copying an organisation chart.
name: Socio-technical coordination of consequential dependencies
non_trigger: Use a direct conversation or temporary collaboration when a lasting team or system reorganisation would cost more.
trigger: Cross-team dependencies cause misunderstandings, delay or incompatible changes.

bearer: Architectural decision allocation across component, product and team boundaries.
criterion: Allow local choices inside explicit shared contracts and escalate or negotiate only decisions that change cross-boundary consequences; preserve a way to resolve conflicts.
name: Distributed decisions constrained by shared consequences
non_trigger: A single team’s common understanding can replace formal delegation structures; avoid review boards for isolated implementation choices.
trigger: Multiple teams need autonomy but share users, data, quality limits or release obligations.

bearer: Claimed necessary relationship between organisational and software structures.
criterion: No deterministic rule mapping an organisation chart to software architecture is admitted; communication and technical structures influence each other under contingent conditions.
name: Deterministic organisational mirroring
non_trigger: Investigate the actual dependency/coordination mechanisms through ESA-034.
trigger: A reorganisation is asserted to guarantee a desired architecture or every structural similarity is treated as inevitable.

bearer: Documentation volume as a candidate architectural quality indicator.
criterion: Document quantity alone is not retained as a proxy for architectural knowledge, correctness or maintenance value.
name: Documentation quantity as architectural evidence
non_trigger: Ask a real consumer to recover a needed decision or check a correspondence using the smallest adequate material.
trigger: Page counts, completed templates or a large repository of records are used as assurance.

bearer: Intended constraints mapped to realised static or dynamic architectural relationships.
criterion: Check a declared, justified architectural constraint against appropriately extracted or observed relationships; attach the relevant baseline, mapping and evidence to each finding.
name: Conformance to a justified, mapped baseline
non_trigger: Use a focused code/configuration review or small dependency check; a universal conformance framework is unnecessary.
trigger: A system depends on a structural or behavioural restriction that implementation changes might violate.

bearer: Deviations between intended, documented and realised architectures over time.
criterion: For a deviation, decide whether the implementation is harmful, the model is stale, the change is authorised improvement or evidence is insufficient; revise the correct object.
name: Adjudication of drift and authorised improvement
non_trigger: Explain and update a simple obsolete rule directly when the improvement and authority are clear; do not force a rollback to satisfy a metric.
trigger: A realised relationship departs from an architectural baseline.

bearer: Potential architectural risk indicators extracted from code, graphs or review text.
criterion: Use a smell or detector output to prioritise investigation, then connect it to actual quality, invariant or change burden before prescribing repair.
name: Architectural smells as defeasible risk indicators
non_trigger: Investigate a concrete recurring failure directly; skip a detector when its noise costs more than manual diagnosis.
trigger: There are enough suspected structural problems that triage may save investigation effort.

bearer: Distinction between recovered architecture and missing design rationale.
criterion: Recovered structure cannot by itself establish the stakeholders, alternatives or rationale behind it; inferred intent must be labelled and corroborated.
name: Recovered structure as a substitute for intended rationale
non_trigger: Retain observed facts, ask a knowledgeable participant or state the intent as unresolved rather than manufacture it.
trigger: A recovered graph or generated description is treated as a replacement for absent decision history.

bearer: Historical model compliance as an unconditional architectural objective.
criterion: Zero departures from any historical model is not admitted as a general quality requirement.
name: Zero deviations from a historical architecture
non_trigger: Adjudicate the rule and change through ESA-038/039, preserving the current protected obligation.
trigger: A historical rule is enforced despite changed requirements or evidence that its violation is an improvement.

bearer: Architecture-level compromises and their temporal costs.
criterion: Identify the specific structural compromise, its current benefit, the future work or recurring penalty it may cause and the plausible cost of remedy; distinguish observed interest from a prediction.
name: Architecture debt distinguished from mere imperfection
non_trigger: Leave a harmless imperfection alone; use an ordinary defect or planned enhancement description when debt adds no explanatory value.
trigger: A known architectural choice is causing or credibly expected to cause recurring change/operation burden.

bearer: Sequences and coexistence states between architectural configurations.
criterion: Plan migration steps that preserve required behaviour and compatibility while old and new structures coexist; include routing/data transitions and an explicit end to temporary arrangements.
name: Incremental migration with coexistence and compatibility
non_trigger: A direct replacement or brief planned outage may be safer and cheaper for a small, low-exposure system.
trigger: A consequential replacement must proceed while service or development continues.

bearer: Continuous or periodic checks on selected architectural properties.
criterion: Use maintained checks to detect changes in selected architectural characteristics, and periodically challenge whether the checks still measure the concern and preserve competing constraints.
name: Revisable fitness functions and continuous evaluation
non_trigger: A manual review or occasional targeted test is adequate when changes are infrequent or the property is poorly automatable.
trigger: Repeated changes threaten a sufficiently observable characteristic and feedback can influence decisions.

bearer: Runtime architectural configurations, monitors, model and control actions.
criterion: Observe the running system, interpret observations in an architecture model, choose among allowed changes and execute them through available effectors; keep system-specific translation explicit.
name: Architecture-based observation and runtime adaptation
non_trigger: Use a stable configuration, an operator procedure or a simple established controller when architecture-level adaptation adds no value.
trigger: Operating variation warrants runtime reconfiguration and appropriate actions are available.

bearer: Admissible architectural transition set and post-change system state.
criterion: Constrain allowed changes by the relevant system and external obligations, then assess the actual post-change state; local metric improvement is evidence for only that metric.
name: Constrained adaptation and post-change assurance
non_trigger: Keep a known-safe static choice or require operator judgement when the admissible change envelope cannot be adequately established.
trigger: Runtime or automated changes can violate an invariant, external commitment or competing quality.

bearer: Self-authorisation claim for metric-driven architectural change.
criterion: An improved local objective neither authorises an architectural change nor establishes its external consequences.
name: Self-authorisation through local metric improvement
non_trigger: Apply independently established constraints and observe the actual consequences through ESA-047.
trigger: A controller or decision-support tool treats its own score as sufficient permission and proof of success.

bearer: Architectural options, abstraction/variation points and temporal cost of change.
criterion: Invest in flexibility when a credible change family and its expected cost justify the present complexity; preserve simpler reversible choices where evidence is weak.
name: Investment in future flexibility proportionate to change hypotheses
non_trigger: Defer the extension or implement the currently needed case directly when later change is tolerable.
trigger: A proposed abstraction, extension point or distributed boundary is justified primarily by future changes.

bearer: Service decomposition and deployment topology, distinct from source-code modularity.
criterion: Select independent deployments where workload, release, failure or ownership needs warrant their distributed-system and operational costs; validate data and interaction independence.
name: Microservices conditional on deployment and operating needs
non_trigger: Use a modular monolith or shared deployment when releases, scaling, permissions and operations largely move together.
trigger: Different parts genuinely need separate release/scaling or bounded operational control and teams can support it.

bearer: Logical modules within a deployment and transitions from distributed to consolidated structure.
criterion: Preserve useful logical boundaries inside a shared deployment, or consolidate services whose separation adds costs without a needed independent capability.
name: Modular monoliths and justified consolidation
non_trigger: A simple unlayered local application may suffice when even internal abstraction has no change or comprehension consumer.
trigger: Shared release, scale, trust or operations make independent deployment unnecessary or harmful.

bearer: Function, platform and external-service composition in a serverless deployment.
criterion: Model provider-managed execution and service dependencies, including data locality, lifecycle, communication, resource and failure assumptions relevant to the workload.
name: Serverless architecture with provider and workload boundaries
non_trigger: Use a simpler long-running process or managed service when latency, state or steady demand makes function decomposition costly.
trigger: A design delegates execution/resource management to a serverless platform.

bearer: Learned components embedded in data, software and organisational processes.
criterion: Include training/serving data, model behaviour, undeclared consumers and feedback paths in architectural reasoning; treat distribution and model changes as potential contract changes.
name: Architecture for learned components and data dependencies
non_trigger: A deterministic rule or isolated advisory component may be simpler when learning adds no justified capability.
trigger: Learned components influence consequential system outputs or are reused by downstream consumers.

bearer: AI-produced architectural representations, options, risk analyses and boundary proposals.
criterion: Use generated alternatives, descriptions or risk suggestions as candidates; independently check their evidence, semantics, metrics and fit to the actual system before relying on them.
name: Evidence-checked AI assistance for architectural work
non_trigger: Use direct human analysis, deterministic extraction or established checks when verification costs exceed the assistance benefit.
trigger: AI assistance could reduce search/drafting effort and adequate validation is available.

bearer: Architectural choices affecting operational and lifecycle resource consequences.
criterion: Declare the sustainability concern and system/lifecycle boundary, then evaluate architectural alternatives against measurable impacts and competing constraints rather than assuming a fashionable deployment is greener.
name: Sustainability as an explicitly bounded architectural concern
non_trigger: Use a targeted operational measurement or omit a specialised control when its impact is negligible and its own cost dominates.
trigger: Energy, emissions, resource use or longer-term maintainability are material stakeholder concerns.

bearer: Architecture methods and governance arrangements applied to a particular system.
criterion: Keep only the architectural control, artefact or coordination mechanism whose consumer and avoided risk justify its cost; choose the smallest coherent arrangement and retire obsolete controls.
name: Proportional governance and retirement of controls
non_trigger: No extra intervention is appropriate when existing shared understanding and ordinary engineering already address the concern adequately.
trigger: Architecture work imposes review, documentation, modelling or coordination cost.

bearer: Superseded umbrella over architectural styles and reference-model concepts.
criterion: The useful warning is retained through separate REST constraints (ESA-065) and service interaction/effect contracts (ESA-066), whose assumptions and consumers differ.
name: Service and REST constraints distinguished from labels
non_trigger: Name and check the actual required interaction property without imposing either complete style.
trigger: A design relies on “service-oriented” or “RESTful” as if the word alone establishes interoperability or quality.

bearer: Architectural reasoning across time, distinct from a mandatory upfront document phase.
criterion: Emergence is not a general exemption from examining architecture-relevant consequences; reason just enough, and revise as the system and knowledge change.
name: Emergence as a reason to omit architectural reasoning
non_trigger: Use timely local reasoning, concrete experiments and brief rationale rather than a speculative full upfront design.
trigger: An evolutionary or agile label is used to avoid considering a consequential interface, quality or migration decision.

bearer: Boundary between architecture-description requirements and realised architecture quality.
criterion: Conformance of an architecture description is not admitted as a certificate that the actual architecture satisfies stakeholder concerns.
name: Description-standard conformance as quality certification
non_trigger: Use the standard for the description purpose and separately establish the selected system-quality claim.
trigger: A standards claim about documentation is offered as proof of performance, security, maintainability or other operating quality.

bearer: Autonomous architecture decision and change process under open-ended requirements.
criterion: No general method for reliable autonomous architecting under evolving open-ended requirements is established by the examined evidence; preserve it as a research question rather than a prohibition or accepted capability.
name: Autonomous architecting under open-ended requirements
non_trigger: Use bounded assistance or a constrained controller with explicit admissible actions and independent evaluation.
trigger: A proposed system is expected to choose, authorise, implement and validate consequential architecture with little or no external judgement.

bearer: Domain model validity and semantic relationships, distinct from physical topology.
criterion: State where a model’s terms and rules are valid, map actual relations to other models, and make required translation or shared meaning explicit.
name: Bounded semantic models and explicit translation
non_trigger: A single shared model and conversation can suffice where meanings genuinely coincide; do not invent contexts solely to match teams.
trigger: Different domains or teams use similar terms with incompatible meanings or need different model evolution.

bearer: Coupling between user interaction and architectural state/control mechanisms.
criterion: Allow a concrete user-interaction concern to change architecture when satisfying it requires system state, control, responsiveness or recoverability beyond visual layout.
name: Usability concerns allowed to reshape architecture
non_trigger: Keep the change in local interface design when it has no substantive architectural implication; the source method itself discards such scenarios.
trigger: A user scenario cannot be met by presentation changes alone.

bearer: Adaptation controller, monitoring model, policy and their revision boundaries.
criterion: Treat changes to sensors, architectural models, adaptation policies and assurance assumptions as consequential changes requiring bounded validation and continuity checks, not as automatically safe self-repair.
name: Safe change of adaptation policies and assurance assumptions
non_trigger: Use a reviewed offline policy change or retain the existing validated configuration where live self-revision adds avoidable risk.
trigger: A running adaptation mechanism or its evidence/decision rules are being revised.

bearer: Design rationale and its historical/propositional status.
criterion: Provide a coherent explanation of why the current design is defensible while separately labelling historical records and reconstructed reasoning; do not make a tidy story into fabricated provenance.
name: Rationalised design explanation distinguished from actual history
non_trigger: A concise explanation marked as reconstructed is better than reconstructing a fictitious complete decision chronology.
trigger: A later consumer needs an understandable design account and the original process was incomplete, iterative or poorly recorded.

bearer: Network interaction style at distributed-hypermedia scope.
criterion: Where its context fits, apply REST’s client/server, stateless interaction, cache, uniform-interface and layered constraints together, with optional code-on-demand and their associated trade-offs.
name: REST interaction constraints
non_trigger: Use a simpler local interface or another protocol/style where its constraints impose costs without those benefits; do not call every HTTP API REST.
trigger: An Internet-scale distributed-hypermedia interaction problem benefits from visibility, intermediaries and independent evolution.

bearer: Service relationship and externally meaningful effects, not merely interface syntax.
criterion: For a service relationship, distinguish awareness/reachability/willingness, the exchanged information/actions and the consequence that the consumer seeks, including policy or contract conditions.
name: Service visibility, interaction and real-world-effect contracts
non_trigger: A direct internal function contract may suffice when there is no separate service/participant relation to manage.
trigger: A consumer relies on another participant’s capability across a service boundary.

bearer: Design of a system or architectural element through requirement allocation and interfaces.
criterion: Use prioritised requirements and constraints to select a consequential element, choose design concepts, allocate responsibilities, define interfaces and refine the resulting obligations; revisit earlier choices when evaluation reveals a problem.
name: Driver-based recursive architectural design
non_trigger: Use a focused local design decision when recursive decomposition would only reproduce the obvious.
trigger: A system or element needs deliberate architectural decomposition and the significant drivers are understood sufficiently to guide a choice.

bearer: Formal component ports, connector roles and glue in the Wright/CSP model.
criterion: When using the Wright/CSP formalism, establish both connector conservatism and deadlock freedom along with port/role compatibility before transferring the theorem’s deadlock-freedom result to an instantiated connector.
name: Connector compatibility under well-formedness constraints
non_trigger: Use an ordinary protocol review or targeted model for a smaller obligation; do not impose Wright on unrelated architectures.
trigger: A connector composition relies specifically on this formal deadlock-freedom guarantee.

bearer: Change request, affected behaviour and requirements history. Requests, contracts, code, data, configuration, manuals and maintenance readiness can all be affected.
criterion: An authorised change objective and explicit preserved or revised obligations can be compared with the actual result.
name: Authorised change intent and obligation revision
non_trigger: A short accepted issue with concrete examples is enough for a bounded low-risk change; reject or defer an unjustified request.
trigger: A request, discovered defect or environmental pressure proposes changing an existing commitment.

bearer: Request intent and actual changed artefacts. Requests, contracts, code, data, configuration, manuals and maintenance readiness can all be affected.
criterion: A mixed change can be described without hiding one purpose or treating a statistic from another taxonomy as comparable.
name: Decision-relevant, edition-aware maintenance classification
non_trigger: Do not label every commit when the label changes no decision; one explanatory sentence may suffice.
trigger: Classification affects estimates, authorisation, reporting or selection of maintenance evidence.

bearer: Consequential code and non-code artefacts within a stated maintenance obligation.
criterion: The consequential non-code objects and their consumers are in the scope, with irrelevant objects omitted explicitly when disputed.
name: Consequential non-code artefact scope
non_trigger: Keep the scope local; no organisation-wide inventory is required when the relevant inputs and consumers are already known.
trigger: A maintenance task depends on consequential state outside conventional source code.

bearer: The actual recipient or continuing maintenance group and its supported work.
criterion: The recipient can perform the relevant supported work, or the remaining capability/support limitation is explicit and acted upon.
name: Demonstrated maintenance readiness and knowledge succession
non_trigger: One representative diagnosis or change can suffice; stable small projects may instead make support limits or retirement explicit, without inventing extra maintainers.
trigger: Initial handover, onboarding, departure, concentration or a new support obligation threatens practical maintenance capability.

bearer: Source revision, build inputs, package versions, configuration and relevant data-state reference. Requests, contracts, code, data, configuration, manuals and maintenance readiness can all be affected.
criterion: Another authorised maintainer can locate the baseline and reproduce the relevant comparison; restoration is separately tested.
name: Identifiable and recoverable maintenance baseline
non_trigger: A versioned file and recorded command can suffice for a local deterministic artefact; retain richer dependencies only where needed.
trigger: An intervention or investigation requires attributing differences or returning to a known state.

bearer: Live service, temporary configuration or patch and follow-up obligation. Requests, contracts, code, data, configuration, manuals and maintenance readiness can all be affected.
criterion: The accepted containment objective is achieved within its loss and authority boundary, with recovery or permanent resolution still owned.
name: Bounded emergency containment and deliberate degradation
non_trigger: Use normal repair or deliberate non-change when urgency is absent; a simple reversible feature disablement can need only proportionate evidence.
trigger: An incident or serious exposure makes ordinary repair timing unsafe and a feasible containment action can reduce harm.

bearer: Classified requests and activity statistics. Requests, contracts, code, data, configuration, manuals and maintenance readiness can all be affected.
criterion: Rejection is observable when mixed purposes or additive/emergency dimensions remain representable rather than forced away.
name: Four categories as a universally exhaustive taxonomy
non_trigger: Use ESME-C002 and declare the edition and classification purpose.
trigger: An audit or metric system attempts to treat four labels as exhaustive and exclusive.

bearer: System-environment relationship and observed user outcomes. Fix the sampled release stream, artefact boundary, organisation and time unit before interpreting a trajectory.
criterion: An identified change in environmental fit has a reasoned response, which may be no change.
name: Environment-sensitive usefulness feedback
non_trigger: For a stable environment, use occasional review or existing user feedback rather than continuous change.
trigger: Evidence of changed environment, user dissatisfaction or new constraints, not age alone.

bearer: Release histories and environmental conditions. Fix the sampled release stream, artefact boundary, organisation and time unit before interpreting a trajectory.
criterion: A decision does not mandate growth or replacement solely from age.
name: Universal growth and inevitable deterioration as prescriptions
non_trigger: Assess actual usefulness and obligations through ESME-C008 instead.
trigger: Someone invokes an evolution law without identifying system class, measure or environment.

bearer: Release sample, size/function/effort measures and data-extraction rules. Fix the sampled release stream, artefact boundary, organisation and time unit before interpreting a trajectory.
criterion: The claim and its planning use have a declared domain and contrary evidence rather than an unqualified law.
name: Population-, metric- and timescale-bounded evolution claims
non_trigger: Use a simple trend with explicit units when it directly answers the decision; no statistical model is mandatory.
trigger: Growth, complexity, effort or decline measurements guide investment or generalisation.

bearer: Maintainer knowledge, workload, change volume and review outcomes. Fix the sampled release stream, artefact boundary, organisation and time unit before interpreting a trajectory.
criterion: The selected workload can be understood and supported by available people, with bottlenecks made explicit.
name: Familiarity and demonstrated maintenance capacity
non_trigger: A small expert-maintained component may need only a direct conversation and modest change cadence.
trigger: Change volume or personnel turnover outpaces demonstrated ability to understand and maintain obligations.

bearer: Historical effort and release-rate observations. Fix the sampled release stream, artefact boundary, organisation and time unit before interpreting a trajectory.
criterion: Forecasts retain uncertainty and do not treat changed conditions as impossible by definition.
name: Invariant organisational work rate as a planning law
non_trigger: Measure local capacity and uncertainty using ESME-C011.
trigger: A plan invokes a universal rate to dismiss changed capability or demand.

bearer: The affected feature and evidence needed for the current decision. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.
criterion: The maintainer can answer the consequential change questions and state remaining uncertainty.
name: Bounded, change-specific comprehension
non_trigger: Inspect the relevant code, test and domain example directly for a small familiar change; avoid mandatory reconstruction of everything.
trigger: A maintainer cannot explain the relevant effect or uncertainty of a proposed intervention.

bearer: Program statements, variable criterion and control/data dependencies. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.
criterion: The result states the criterion and model and is not represented as an exact minimal slice or a complete account of all real effects.
name: Criterion-relative static slicing
non_trigger: Direct inspection suffices for a small obvious dependence; no slicing tool is required.
trigger: A consequential comprehension or impact question benefits from model-based relevance beyond a single observed run.

bearer: Trace, instrumentation, inputs and runtime configuration. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.
criterion: The explanation is supported for the observed execution and does not become a universal absence-of-effect claim.
name: Execution-conditioned dynamic slicing and tracing
non_trigger: Use direct reproduction or existing logs when adequate; omit instrumentation when no relevant run can be obtained.
trigger: Observed behaviour or a concrete failure requires an execution-specific explanation.

bearer: Implementation, domain rules, historical decisions and tacit operational knowledge. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.
criterion: The recovered explanation supports a concrete maintenance decision and identifies uncertain or contested intent.
name: Corroborated design and intent recovery
non_trigger: Ask a knowledgeable maintainer a focused question rather than commissioning a comprehensive recovery model.
trigger: Undocumented behaviour or lost intent makes structural reconstruction insufficient.

bearer: Documentation and its source artefact/version. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.
criterion: A consumer can use the description to perform the intended task; its version and limits are visible.
name: Faithful redocumentation with an actual consumer
non_trigger: A checked example, code comment or targeted note can replace a large document.
trigger: A useful explanation is missing, stale or inaccessible to an actual consumer.

bearer: Use source, generated artefacts, build/configuration state, execution traces, relevant history and rationale where each is needed to answer Q.
criterion: A recovered model is not counted as an implemented or validated change, and any real transformation has its own evidence and authority boundary.
name: Recovery and redocumentation are not operative transformation
non_trigger: Ordinary descriptions suffice for unambiguous local work; a taxonomy table is unnecessary.
trigger: A recovery or modernisation activity is proposed, evaluated or handed off.

bearer: Whole-system knowledge claims. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.
criterion: A local change may proceed on justified local evidence while unknown remote areas remain declared.
name: Exhaustive comprehension before every change
non_trigger: Use ESME-C013, widening only on consequential uncertainty.
trigger: A process imposes global understanding without a decision-relevant trigger.

bearer: Feature description, code locations, calls, traces and change history. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.
criterion: Candidate locations are confirmed against the feature and false leads are recorded or discarded.
name: Feature-location hypotheses and interactive refinement
non_trigger: A direct known location or maintainer pointer avoids a specialised search workflow.
trigger: A change request describes a feature whose implementation is not already known.

bearer: Extracted components/relations, execution observations and build mapping. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.
criterion: The relevant conclusion states supporting views, discrepancies and remaining uncertainty.
name: Question-selected views and reconciliation of discrepancies
non_trigger: One adequate direct view can settle a local question without a fusion framework.
trigger: A single view leaves a consequential question unresolved or independent views disagree.

bearer: Code, data, interfaces, configuration, builds, documentation and consumers. Include code, APIs, data, configuration, generated artefacts, builds, release combinations and downstream consumers.
criterion: The proposed boundary has a stated basis and uncertainty, and known consequential escapes change the scope or decision rather than being ignored.
name: Revisable impact boundary with proportionate counterexample challenge
non_trigger: Local review is sufficient when a defensible dependency boundary makes wider effects immaterial.
trigger: An edit can propagate outside its immediate location or alter a relied-on contract.

bearer: Version-history transactions and recommended entities. Include code, APIs, data, configuration, generated artefacts, builds, release combinations and downstream consumers.
criterion: Suggested entities are either justified as relevant or dismissed; absent suggestions do not certify independence.
name: Interpreted historical co-change evidence
non_trigger: Skip mining for new code, sparse history or an obvious direct dependency.
trigger: History contains sufficiently comparable changes and a maintainer needs likely impact leads.

bearer: Mined transactions and candidate dependency edge. Include code, APIs, data, configuration, generated artefacts, builds, release combinations and downstream consumers.
criterion: A mined edge remains provisional until its meaning is established.
name: Co-change correlation proves necessary dependency
non_trigger: Inspect the proposed relation under ESME-C023 and seek direct dependency evidence.
trigger: An impact tool’s history score is used as operative authority.

bearer: Build scripts, resources, schemas, generated code, package inputs and tool versions. Include code, APIs, data, configuration, generated artefacts, builds, release combinations and downstream consumers.
criterion: Impact reasoning identifies relevant edge kinds and their limits, including consequential non-code propagation.
name: Typed, multi-artefact dependency propagation
non_trigger: A recorded explicit command and input list suffice where there is no indirect generation or configuration.
trigger: Non-source inputs or generators influence the target behaviour or regression selection.

bearer: Public API, binary interface, protocol, persistent representation and supported versions. Include code, APIs, data, configuration, generated artefacts, builds, release combinations and downstream consumers.
criterion: Supported interactions remain valid or consumers have an authorised transition path with explicit limitations.
name: Supported-observer compatibility obligations
non_trigger: Internal changes with no consequential external observer need no compatibility programme.
trigger: An interface, schema or protocol is relied on outside the edited component.

bearer: Version labels and actual package/API behaviour. Include code, APIs, data, configuration, generated artefacts, builds, release combinations and downstream consumers.
criterion: A label is distinguished from evidence of the relevant compatibility property.
name: Version labels prove compatibility
non_trigger: Use the label as a triage signal and verify consequential interactions.
trigger: An update policy infers behaviour from a label without checking the applicable contract.

bearer: Base/left/right/merge versions, build definitions and behavioural interactions. Include code, APIs, data, configuration, generated artefacts, builds, release combinations and downstream consumers.
criterion: The merged state satisfies the jointly accepted objectives or an explicit conflict is resolved.
name: Semantic validation of concurrent and merged changes
non_trigger: Ordinary compilation and targeted tests suffice for clearly independent low-risk changes.
trigger: Changes overlap semantically or one branch alters assumptions used by another.

bearer: Supported releases, feature/configuration choices, platform/tool versions and consumers. Include code, APIs, data, configuration, generated artefacts, builds, release combinations and downstream consumers.
criterion: Evidence and limitations can be mapped to the supported combinations and obsolete obligations are retired.
name: Scoped support of concurrent versions and variants
non_trigger: One explicitly supported configuration needs no elaborate matrix; retire unsupported variants transparently.
trigger: Several versions, build options, platforms or deployment variants remain supported.

bearer: Pre/post implementation and relevant external context. Use exact pre/post code, language/tool versions and relevant runtime, persistence and external-interface context.
criterion: The claimed equivalence is stated relative to the observer and supported by appropriate evidence.
name: Observer-relative preservation claims
non_trigger: For an isolated pure function, input/output and exceptional behaviour may be an adequate observer; no universal observer inventory is mandatory.
trigger: A transformation is justified as non-functional or structure-only.

bearer: Transformation rule, input program, language semantics and engine version. Use exact pre/post code, language/tool versions and relevant runtime, persistence and external-interface context.
criterion: Applicability is demonstrated or transformation is refused/narrowed; exceptions remain explicit.
name: Applicable transformation rules and preconditions
non_trigger: Direct review of a small transformation can replace a general engine when its conditions are simple.
trigger: A transformation’s correctness depends on names, bindings, inheritance, types or other structural conditions.

bearer: The selected transformation engine, implementation and version.
criterion: The relevant engine behaviour has bounded validation evidence and known exclusions.
name: Validation of transformation-engine implementation
non_trigger: For a small trusted operation, review its concrete output rather than building a universal tool-validation campaign.
trigger: A transformation engine is new, changed, historically faulty or used outside its validated envelope.

bearer: The actual transformed candidate and the observations required of it.
criterion: The exact candidate has evidence for its intended and preserved obligations, with unresolved failures visible.
name: Validation of the actual transformed candidate
non_trigger: A small reviewed diff and a targeted check may be enough; no universal demand for multiple expensive validators.
trigger: Any consequential restructuring, generated patch or composed change is proposed for acceptance.

bearer: Structure, expected change scenarios and intervention effort. Use exact pre/post code, language/tool versions and relevant runtime, persistence and external-interface context.
criterion: A structural investment has a task-specific benefit hypothesis, cost/uncertainty account and a continuation, revision or stop decision based on applicable observations.
name: Task-costed structural improvement with bounded payoff review
non_trigger: Leave adequate stable structure alone; a small relevant transformation and one representative task can suffice without an economic dashboard.
trigger: Repeated or credible upcoming work is materially hindered by the current structure and a feasible change may improve it.

bearer: Metric definition, affected structure and real maintenance tasks. Use exact pre/post code, language/tool versions and relevant runtime, persistence and external-interface context.
criterion: Metric movement is not reported as benefit unless the relevant outcome is also supported.
name: Task-validated maintainability measurements
non_trigger: Direct evidence of difficult changes or a small review may dominate metric dashboards.
trigger: A metric might reveal a bottleneck not already understood.

bearer: Transformation label and resulting code. Use exact pre/post code, language/tool versions and relevant runtime, persistence and external-interface context.
criterion: The acceptance decision refers to preservation and benefit evidence rather than a label.
name: Catalogue compliance as a maintenance property
non_trigger: Use ESME-C030–031 without requiring a named catalogue entry.
trigger: A process rewards transformations performed rather than obligations preserved or cost reduced.

bearer: Legacy outputs, tests, data examples and requirement interpretation. Bind tests, results, build inputs, artefact identity, environment, deployed versions and relevant data state.
criterion: Observed behaviour is distinguished from authorised expectations; a golden output is not automatically an immutable obligation.
name: Characterisation as descriptive evidence, not automatic specification
non_trigger: A focused example or domain review may suffice instead of broad snapshot generation.
trigger: Important undocumented behaviour makes a change risky.

bearer: New objective, preservation set, tests and other evidence. Bind tests, results, build inputs, artefact identity, environment, deployed versions and relevant data state.
criterion: Acceptance can explain both the justified difference and the justified continuity.
name: Intentional differences and independently retained obligations
non_trigger: One test may address both obligations if its distinct assertions and coverage are clear; no separate team is inherently required.
trigger: Any intervention changes or risks a relied-on behaviour.

bearer: The provenance and scope of the observation or acceptance criterion.
criterion: The acceptance claim distinguishes observed passage from the supported intended and preserved obligations.
name: Oracle provenance and justified expected outcomes
non_trigger: A trusted narrow assertion may suffice for a simple obligation; do not build a specification language merely for appearance.
trigger: Test results support a change decision or a test expectation itself changes.

bearer: Original/changed program, existing test suite and selection dependencies. Bind tests, results, build inputs, artefact identity, environment, deployed versions and relevant data state.
criterion: Selected-suite rationale and exclusions are visible; unsupported change kinds trigger fallback.
name: Assumption-bounded regression-test selection
non_trigger: Run the full affordable suite; do not add selection complexity when it saves little.
trigger: Running the whole available suite has material cost and sound selection can be justified.

bearer: Test set, order, duration estimates and failure relevance. Bind tests, results, build inputs, artefact identity, environment, deployed versions and relevant data state.
criterion: The ordering objective is stated and omitted tests, if any, remain known.
name: Action-relevant regression-test prioritisation
non_trigger: Keep the existing order when the suite is cheap or priority estimates are unreliable.
trigger: A time-constrained test run benefits from earlier actionable failures.

bearer: Mutants, tests, fault model and targeted behaviour. Bind tests, results, build inputs, artefact identity, environment, deployed versions and relevant data state.
criterion: A surviving relevant mutant yields a useful test/observation or an explained non-obligation.
name: Mutation-based challenge of test sensitivity
non_trigger: Add a targeted real-fault regression case or review a missing assertion rather than run broad mutation campaigns.
trigger: A consequential preservation obligation may be weakly exercised by the current tests.

bearer: The implementations, input domain and comparison interpretation used by differential evidence.
criterion: Observed differences are classified as intended, erroneous or unresolved rather than automatically counted as bugs.
name: Differential comparison under a justified reference relation
non_trigger: Use direct expected results for simple cases; no duplicate implementation is required where it adds less evidence than it costs.
trigger: A credible reference exists and executions can be made comparable.

bearer: The justified relation between transformed inputs and expected output relations.
criterion: The relation is checked for stated cases, with no claim that satisfaction proves arbitrary output correctness.
name: Justified metamorphic relations as partial oracles
non_trigger: Use ordinary assertions when expected results are cheap; do not invent weak relations to inflate a test count.
trigger: Exact expected results are difficult but a relevant mathematical or domain relation is credible.

bearer: Patch, test suite, harness, environment and accepted requirements. Bind tests, results, build inputs, artefact identity, environment, deployed versions and relevant data state.
criterion: The reported conclusion does not exceed the actual tested obligation and environment.
name: Passing all selected tests proves correctness
non_trigger: Make a scoped test claim and add only the missing consequential evidence, rather than demand impossible universal testing.
trigger: A release or generated patch is accepted solely because a finite suite is green.

bearer: Source, compiler, packaging tools, dependencies, environment and released artefact. Bind tests, results, build inputs, artefact identity, environment, deployed versions and relevant data state.
criterion: A relevant rebuild or exact identity comparison succeeds, or its nondeterminism and limitations are explicit.
name: Build provenance and relevant reproducibility
non_trigger: For a directly interpreted single file, version identity and execution environment may be enough; do not mandate byte-identical builds without a consumer.
trigger: Attribution, support, archival reuse or supply-chain checks depend on connecting source and delivered artefacts.

bearer: Integrated revisions, build/test results and responsible maintainers. Bind tests, results, build inputs, artefact identity, environment, deployed versions and relevant data state.
criterion: Integration failures are attributed and resolved or consciously deferred before relying on the combined state.
name: Actionable integration feedback
non_trigger: A small serially maintained artefact can use direct build/test checks without a dedicated service or fixed cadence.
trigger: Concurrent changes or delayed integration conceal incompatibilities.

bearer: Release candidate, control, traffic population, data/configuration and monitoring. Bind tests, results, build inputs, artefact identity, environment, deployed versions and relevant data state.
criterion: Expansion is justified by relevant observations; missing signal is not treated as a pass.
name: Observable, actionable staged exposure
non_trigger: Use direct release with proportionate checks for low-impact changes, or offline rehearsal where live exposure is unsafe.
trigger: Production-only uncertainties can be investigated with genuinely limited and reversible exposure.

bearer: The remaining recovery and forward-repair options for the actual effect history.
criterion: At the consequential action boundary, the promised remaining recovery/containment route is feasible for the relevant state, or the residual loss is explicitly accepted by the appropriate decision maker.
name: Effect-aware recovery, forward repair and changing returnability
non_trigger: A pure reversible local edit may need only one verified return path; acceptable reconstruction or forward repair can replace elaborate rollback machinery.
trigger: A change or exposure can leave consequential state or lose an existing recovery option.

bearer: Fault location, affected behaviour and support horizon. Baseline includes domain behaviour, live data, old/new implementations, routing and temporary synchronisation mechanisms.
criterion: The fault is corrected and preserved obligations are evidenced within the stated boundary.
name: Bounded local repair as an alternative to restructuring
non_trigger: No change is cheaper where the reported behaviour is acceptable; a focused correction is cheaper than modernisation when adequate.
trigger: A local fault has a justified impact boundary and no demonstrated need for broad redesign.

bearer: Existing service, domain behaviour, technology dependencies and support capacity. Baseline includes domain behaviour, live data, old/new implementations, routing and temporary synchronisation mechanisms.
criterion: A continue/change/retire decision is supported by actual value and risk rather than age alone.
name: Legacy value distinguished from technical age
non_trigger: Continue operation with existing support when useful and adequately maintainable.
trigger: A system is labelled legacy or obsolete as grounds for investment.

bearer: Existing capability, candidate host/platform/implementation and transition obligations. Baseline includes domain behaviour, live data, old/new implementations, routing and temporary synchronisation mechanisms.
criterion: The chosen branch has a defensible advantage over feasible no-change, repair or migration alternatives.
name: Obligation- and lifecycle-based intervention selection
non_trigger: Compare only credible alternatives; a short repair-versus-replace decision can suffice.
trigger: Current maintenance no longer meets justified needs or costs warrant reconsideration.

bearer: Legacy/successor components, seam, routing, shared data and temporary adapters. Baseline includes domain behaviour, live data, old/new implementations, routing and temporary synchronisation mechanisms.
criterion: A slice of responsibility is actually transferred and temporary coexistence remains controlled.
name: Incremental responsibility transfer at viable seams
non_trigger: A small system may be cheaper to replace atomically; no migration when existing service remains adequate.
trigger: Useful seams permit partial replacement and intermediate states preserve required service/data semantics.

bearer: Complete successor, cutover state, consumers and recovery resources. Baseline includes domain behaviour, live data, old/new implementations, routing and temporary synchronisation mechanisms.
criterion: The cutover is authorised against endpoint and conversion evidence, not just successor tests.
name: Rehearsed quiescent or atomic cutover
non_trigger: Prefer bounded repair or incremental transfer where they meet obligations with less risk.
trigger: The system is small or separability is poor, downtime is acceptable, or dual operation creates intolerable inconsistency.

bearer: Old/new data, mapping rules, transaction history and reconciliation evidence. Baseline includes domain behaviour, live data, old/new implementations, routing and temporary synchronisation mechanisms.
criterion: The converted state has justified meaning and authority within a declared scope, with divergence and unresolved losses surfaced.
name: Data-conversion meaning, authority and reconciliation
non_trigger: For stateless replacement this is not triggered; a simple verified bijective conversion may need only direct checks.
trigger: Schema, encoding, representation or ownership changes can alter persisted meaning.

bearer: Identify both implementations, mappings, data versions, routing, write ownership, temporary adapters and relevant consumer versions.
criterion: Queries and converted states meet the declared mapping, or losses and unsupported rewrites block the preservation claim.
name: Schema mappings, information loss and inverse limits
non_trigger: Use a direct checked migration for a simple bijective mapping; a full workbench is unnecessary.
trigger: Schema/data representation changes affect persistent meaning or old-version access.

bearer: Versions of readers/writers, schema, protocol, configuration and shared state. Baseline includes domain behaviour, live data, old/new implementations, routing and temporary synchronisation mechanisms.
criterion: Only validated version/state combinations are active; unsupported skew triggers containment or a different route.
name: Reachable mixed-version and schema compatibility
non_trigger: Use an atomic stop-and-switch when mixed versions offer no justified advantage and downtime is acceptable.
trigger: Rolling upgrades, data conversion or partial migration create old/new participants at the same time.

bearer: Temporary migration/coexistence machinery and its remaining obligations.
criterion: Removal or declared completion has evidence that the relevant old-path obligations are discharged or explicitly reassigned; remaining supported coexistence and cost are not hidden.
name: Coexistence cost, completion witness and scaffold retirement
non_trigger: No scaffold is needed for a genuine one-step transfer; justified permanent coexistence can be reclassified rather than falsely called completed migration.
trigger: Migration creates temporary coexistence, or completion/removal of an old path is proposed.

bearer: Replacement decision and realistic alternatives. Baseline includes domain behaviour, live data, old/new implementations, routing and temporary synchronisation mechanisms.
criterion: Replacement remains admissible when it meets obligations better than available alternatives.
name: Rewrites are always wrong
non_trigger: Compare repair, incremental and atomic alternatives under ESME-C052.
trigger: A viable replacement is rejected solely by a slogan.

bearer: Current and candidate platforms, relevant tooling and maintainer skills. Baseline includes domain behaviour, live data, old/new implementations, routing and temporary synchronisation mechanisms.
criterion: The selected platform is justified by concrete requirements, not release date.
name: Age or novelty alone as the intervention rule
non_trigger: Retain the existing platform when obligations and support are satisfied.
trigger: A migration is justified principally by novelty or fashion.

bearer: Code revision, persistent and external effect history. Baseline includes domain behaviour, live data, old/new implementations, routing and temporary synchronisation mechanisms.
criterion: Recovery claims distinguish source rollback from restored data and accepted irreversible consequences.
name: Reverting code reverses the system
non_trigger: For a genuinely isolated file-only effect, code reversion can be adequate; otherwise use ESME-C049.
trigger: A rollout or migration changes data, schemas, messages, payments or other external state.

bearer: Debt condition, cause, affected future change and support horizon. A debt item links a concrete design/implementation condition to affected future work and its economic context.
criterion: An item states how and when it imposes additional cost; disappearance of that scenario can retire the item.
name: Causally specified future-maintenance debt
non_trigger: Do not create debt items for disliked code with no relevant future-cost mechanism.
trigger: A structural choice plausibly increases future change cost or blocks justified evolution.

bearer: Debt item, supporting observations, cost estimates and decision history. A debt item links a concrete design/implementation condition to affected future work and its economic context.
criterion: The record changes or supports a prioritisation decision and is refreshed or retired as context changes.
name: Actionable debt records with a consumer
non_trigger: A tracked issue or brief decision note can replace a dedicated register; delete records whose liability has vanished.
trigger: A significant liability risks being forgotten, misunderstood or shifted across teams.

bearer: Maintenance options, benefits, cost horizon and uncertainty. A debt item links a concrete design/implementation condition to affected future work and its economic context.
criterion: A priority decision explains trade-offs, uncertainty and the evidence that could reverse it.
name: Contingent maintenance economics and opportunity cost
non_trigger: A qualitative ordered comparison is sufficient when numerical estimates would be fictitious.
trigger: Competing repairs, features, structural improvements or retirement choices draw on limited resources.

bearer: Deferred liability, prospective demand and revisit condition. A debt item links a concrete design/implementation condition to affected future work and its economic context.
criterion: Deferral is an explicit justified choice with a relevant trigger rather than forgotten work.
name: Option-preserving deferral and deliberate non-repayment
non_trigger: Do nothing beyond existing observation when there is no live liability; immediate repair dominates when an obligation is already breached.
trigger: Future change demand is uncertain, interest is small, or the system may retire before repayment benefits arise.

bearer: Cost allocation, support promises and affected stakeholders. A debt item links a concrete design/implementation condition to affected future work and its economic context.
criterion: The decision states material shifted costs and how affected parties can act on the information.
name: Visible cost bearers and legitimate maintenance prioritisation
non_trigger: A direct agreement can suffice; no universal committee or separate owner per item is required.
trigger: A local benefit shifts material work or obligations to other teams, future maintainers or external consumers.

bearer: Debt inventory and maintenance budget. A debt item links a concrete design/implementation condition to affected future work and its economic context.
criterion: Debt reduction is not accepted as benefit without an affected-value account.
name: Zero technical debt as the objective
non_trigger: Prioritise justified liabilities and retire irrelevant ones under ESME-C062–059.
trigger: A programme treats the debt count as a target to drive to zero.

bearer: Index, scoring model and future tasks. A debt item links a concrete design/implementation condition to affected future work and its economic context.
criterion: A score is identified as a proxy and does not independently certify savings.
name: A universal maintainability index proves future savings
non_trigger: Use actual change history, qualitative estimates or bounded experiments and disclose uncertainty.
trigger: A decision claims certain savings from score improvement without task evidence.

bearer: Bind before/after source, language/tool version, configuration and persistent representations to the actual applied transformation.
criterion: No unconditional payoff is inferred from a cleaner representation alone.
name: Clean structure as a guarantee of maintenance benefit
non_trigger: Keep a harmless structure or make a bounded repair.
trigger: Adjudicate when a structural metric or catalogue label is offered as sufficient benefit evidence.

bearer: Change rationale, baseline references and accepted trade-offs. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.
criterion: A successor can connect a relevant constraint to its reason and identify when that reason no longer holds.
name: Retained rationale through actual future use
non_trigger: An adjacent comment, issue or concise handover may suffice; do not duplicate rationale in unconsumed documents.
trigger: Loss of intent would materially obstruct future change, support or retirement.

bearer: Change requests, affected components and decision responsibilities. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.
criterion: A relevant request or conflict can reach someone able and authorised to decide or explicitly decline.
name: Scoped ownership and change coordination
non_trigger: One maintainer can hold several roles; collaborative ownership is adequate when responsibility remains actionable.
trigger: Multiple contributors or support paths create ambiguity about acceptance, review or incident response.

bearer: Support promises, workload, available people and tooling. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.
criterion: Support expectations match an actionable capacity plan or clearly announced limitation.
name: Sustainable and willing maintenance support
non_trigger: Reduce nonessential scope or state a limited support policy rather than add complex automation by default.
trigger: Demand, dependency obligations or turnover exceed sustainable support capability.

bearer: Commit history, authorship assumptions and demonstrated expertise. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.
criterion: The estimate is accompanied by checks of actual capability and omitted knowledge.
name: Knowledge-concentration metrics as fallible prompts
non_trigger: Ask maintainers directly or exercise a handover when feasible; no metric is required.
trigger: A project needs to assess continuity and history can offer a useful first approximation.

bearer: Dependency manifests, resolved versions, support status and affected uses. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.
criterion: A consequential dependency change has a justified action or deferral and an explicit support/compatibility account.
name: Obligation-based dependency viability and response
non_trigger: Use a small explicit dependency list and targeted check for a bounded artefact; no ecosystem-wide graph is inherently necessary.
