trigger: A dependency changes, loses support or creates a relevant defect/security obligation.

bearer: Include code, API, schema, protocol, configuration, build, policy and relevant ownership/deployment state rather than a universal source-file-only graph.
criterion: Known affected consumers receive actionable information or an inability to reach them constrains release.
name: Discovery of affected downstream consumers
non_trigger: For a private bounded use with no external consumer, direct coordination with the local caller may suffice.
trigger: A public or shared behaviour, data format, dependency or support promise changes.

bearer: Release notes, support policy, client dependencies and transition instructions. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.
criterion: The relevant consumer can determine required action and remaining support/transition limits; merely publishing a notice is not counted as successful transfer.
name: Consumer-directed, actionable change communication
non_trigger: A direct agreement with the sole consumer may suffice; no broad notice is needed for a truly private effect.
trigger: A change affects consumer obligations, compatibility, support or availability.

bearer: Resource, API version, support policy, deprecation date and possible sunset date. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.
criterion: The announced state and implications are unambiguous to the intended consumer.
name: Deprecation signalling separated from shutdown
non_trigger: A documented support statement may suffice outside HTTP; no header is required where it has no consumer.
trigger: An interface or service is being superseded, losing guarantees or approaching shutdown.

bearer: Service endpoints, users, data, credentials/access, support promises and retained records. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.
criterion: Operational termination and surviving preservation/support arrangements are evidenced separately.
name: Responsible servicing phaseout and retirement
non_trigger: Continue a stable low-cost service when retirement would strand justified obligations; close simple unused artefacts with proportionate checks.
trigger: The software is no longer useful, supportable or justified relative to alternatives.

bearer: Source, dependencies, documentation, data rights and optional executable environment. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.
criterion: The specified historical object can be retrieved or relevant execution reproduced within stated limitations.
name: Purpose-specific historical preservation
non_trigger: Retain a source snapshot and rationale when execution is unnecessary; avoid indefinitely operating a service solely to preserve history.
trigger: Historical analysis, compliance, research reproduction or future revival justifies retained artefacts after active use.

bearer: Package popularity, dependency reach and maintainer capacity. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.
criterion: Continuity claims use actual support evidence rather than download counts alone.
name: Popularity guarantees dependency continuity
non_trigger: Check actual support/capacity and feasible alternatives under ESME-C072 and 068.
trigger: A dependency is accepted without continuity consideration because many projects use it.

bearer: Current capability, support horizon and environmental assumptions. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.
criterion: A no-change decision states why obligations remain met and what evidence would prompt reconsideration.
name: Deliberate continued usefulness without change
non_trigger: This is the cheap path itself; review existing signals rather than create permanent change machinery.
trigger: No demonstrated defect, adaptation need or investment opportunity outweighs change risk and cost.

bearer: Remaining expertise, recoverable design knowledge and feasible change classes. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.
criterion: The practical feasibility of renewed evolution is investigated, not decided solely by a lifecycle diagram.
name: Transition to servicing is effectively irreversible
non_trigger: Assess actual knowledge recovery and replacement choices rather than require a stage label.
trigger: A long-lived system can receive patches but no longer support broad justified evolution economically.

bearer: Generated diff, issue interpretation, tests, harness and environment. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.
criterion: Accepted claims identify repaired obligations and residual uncertainty; unsupported additions are removed or authorised.
name: Generated repairs remain candidates until justified acceptance
non_trigger: A direct human correction may dominate; use the same substantive obligations regardless of who authored the patch.
trigger: A repair or evolution suggestion is generated by a search system, model or agent.

bearer: Execution harness, environment, selected tests, exit conditions and recorded results. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.
criterion: The harness distinguishes relevant known pass/fail controls and binds results to the intended artefact.
name: Validation of the evaluation harness itself
non_trigger: A simple transparent command with known checks may need only a small sanity test rather than a framework audit.
trigger: A harness is new, changed, migrated or relied on for a consequential acceptance claim.

bearer: Benchmark tasks, public history, model versions and evaluation settings. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.
criterion: Evaluation conclusions distinguish the observed benchmark result from uncertain transfer and contamination.
name: Benchmark identity, leakage and transfer boundaries
non_trigger: Use a bounded private or newly authored representative task evaluation where feasible; disclose limits rather than invent clean provenance.
trigger: Benchmark results justify deployment claims or compare automation approaches.

bearer: Issue statement, reference PR, changed tests and alternative patches. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.
criterion: Differences are classified as required, permitted, irrelevant, erroneous or unresolved with reasons.
name: Issue, reference patch and test objective alignment
non_trigger: A precise issue and focused test can suffice; no LLM checker is inherently required.
trigger: Generated repair, benchmark construction or legacy acceptance relies on a reference patch as expected truth.

bearer: Human tasks, model calls, review effort, compute and accepted outcomes. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.
criterion: The benefit claim includes relevant total work and uncertainty rather than generation speed alone.
name: End-to-end automation outcome and cost evaluation
non_trigger: A small representative paired trial or observed task sample may suffice; no grand benchmark is required.
trigger: Automation adoption is justified as saving maintenance effort or increasing useful output.

bearer: Automation configuration and supporting evaluation evidence. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.
criterion: Reused evidence states why its assumptions still hold; affected claims are revalidated or narrowed.
name: Version-bound automation evidence and revalidation
non_trigger: Do not rerun everything for an irrelevant metadata change; use targeted revalidation of affected claims.
trigger: A model, engine, prompt strategy, hardware or evaluation context changes in a way relevant to prior evidence.

bearer: Model, quantisation, hardware, repair instances and resource measurements. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.
criterion: The chosen configuration meets the stated resource and validated outcome constraints.
name: Repair automation resource trade-offs
non_trigger: A simpler deterministic tool or human repair can dominate model tuning for a small task.
trigger: Resource-limited repair automation makes memory, energy or time consequential.

bearer: Base/parent/merged program, generated tests or build-conflict patterns. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.
criterion: A detected interaction has scoped supporting evidence and a disposition rather than automatic rejection or a universal conflict-free guarantee.
name: Bounded automated semantic-conflict detection
non_trigger: Manual joint review and focused integration tests may be enough; clean noninteracting changes need no special tool.
trigger: Concurrent changes have plausible semantic interference that targeted automation can help expose.

bearer: Training/serving data, features, model, code, pipeline and configuration. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.
criterion: The impact claim covers relevant non-code/model dependencies or explicitly marks unknowns.
name: Learned-system data, model and configuration dependencies
non_trigger: Ordinary code/configuration analysis is enough when no learned or changing data dependency is present.
trigger: A learned component or data pipeline influences supported behaviour.

bearer: Data distribution, model, feedback channels and accepted outcome criteria. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.
criterion: A material shift triggers justified re-evaluation or a narrowed claim, not automatic retraining.
name: Drift-sensitive evidence and preserved-obligation review
non_trigger: For a stable deterministic computation, ordinary version-bound regression may suffice.
trigger: A learned or environment-sensitive service has a live obligation whose validity depends on changing distributions or feedback.

bearer: Documents, configuration, datasets, schemas, build recipes and generated outputs. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.
criterion: Validation addresses the artefact’s actual obligation and the effects it can propagate.
name: Operative validation of non-code artefacts
non_trigger: A factual documentation correction may need reader/source verification, not an entire executable test suite.
trigger: A non-code edit can alter buildability, operation, user guidance, data semantics or model behaviour.

bearer: The acceptance decision and execution powers for a concrete intervention.
criterion: The real acceptance and action stay within the delegated object, scope and capability; generated insight or test success does not enlarge them.
name: Bounded acceptance and execution authority
non_trigger: One competent authorised actor may perform all functions for a bounded change; no separate human, meeting or AI-specific approval is implied.
trigger: An actor or automated tool proposes, accepts or executes a change, especially when these functions cross authority boundaries.

bearer: Accepted generated changes, later maintenance tasks, regressions and total lifecycle costs. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.
criterion: No universal benefit asserted; later tasks and regressions would be needed to resolve the claim.
name: Long-term net maintainability benefit of AI-assisted evolution
non_trigger: Run bounded adoption with follow-up evidence; do not assert a long-term benefit absent an adequate horizon and comparator.
trigger: A decision generalises short-run scores or time savings to multi-release lifecycle benefit.

bearer: Automated workflow, generated changes and live obligations. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.
criterion: Delegation remains scoped and its consequences observed; success in a task does not expand its own authority.
name: Universal autonomous maintenance without residual review or authority
non_trigger: Delegate a bounded class with explicit conditions and monitor actual outcomes; human review need not be ceremonial or applied identically to every case.
trigger: A benchmark or demonstration is used to justify unrestricted self-directed production maintenance.

bearer: Legacy behaviour, actual reliance and current requirements. Bind tests, results, build inputs, artefact identity, environment, deployed versions and relevant data state.
criterion: Each preserved or changed behaviour has a justified status and affected consumers are considered.
name: Every historical behaviour must be preserved
non_trigger: Retain relevant promises and authorise justified revisions under ESME-C001 and 034.
trigger: A characterisation test or compatibility argument blocks correction of an obsolete, accidental or harmful behaviour.

bearer: A proposed revision of a maintenance method or oracle relative to the preceding obligation.
criterion: The revision and any change of obligation have a bounded non-circular warrant; unchanged obligations remain in force and the successor does not grant itself wider authority.
name: Non-circular, authorised revision of maintenance methods and oracles
non_trigger: Keep an adequate method or remove an unused control; independent warrant need not mean a different person or an infallible external oracle.
trigger: The method is failing or disproportionately costly, technology changes, or a candidate proposes to revise the expectation by which it will be judged.

bearer: Identify repository/task baseline, tool/model version, prompts/configuration relevant to evaluation, tests and data/model/policy artefacts. Record benchmark version and excluded cases.
criterion: The conclusion preserves both observed harms and supported benefits within their populations.
name: Human-only maintenance is universally superior
non_trigger: Use whichever simple human/tool combination is supported for the actual task, including no automation.
trigger: Adjudicate when a negative experiment is used to forbid all maintenance automation.

bearer: Identify repository/task baseline, tool/model version, prompts/configuration relevant to evaluation, tests and data/model/policy artefacts. Record benchmark version and excluded cases.
criterion: The packet exports an unresolved claim, not an unconditional audit obligation or a declaration of impossibility.
name: Reliable unattended repository-scale maintenance as a general capability
non_trigger: Use bounded automation with explicit constraints, or an ordinary authorised maintainer when evidence is insufficient.
trigger: A general unattended-maintenance claim is used to remove oversight or transfer responsibility.

bearer: Identify the system/configuration being changed and any non-code artefact needed to interpret the request. A source commit alone may omit deployed data and obligations.
criterion: The decision is adequately authorised and informed whether or not a meeting occurs.
name: A formal change board for every change
non_trigger: A direct authorised maintainer decision can suffice for a bounded change.
trigger: Adjudicate when the presence of a board is treated as the maintenance property itself.

bearer: The cross-stage binding between intent, subject, candidate, evidence and authorised action.
criterion: The evidence actually consumed and the action actually taken concern the same scoped candidate, obligations and authority; a detected mismatch blocks only the unsupported use.
name: Cross-stage change–evidence–action coherence
non_trigger: One visible issue, exact diff and direct check can establish the binding in a local change; no separate contract document or registry is required.
trigger: Evidence or decisions pass among stages, tools or actors, or concurrent work can change the subject before action.

bearer: The applicability of downstream claims to their consequential supporting assumptions.
criterion: No affected claim retains unqualified operative force outside its evidence envelope; unaffected evidence remains usable.
name: Assumption-indexed evidence invalidation across mechanisms
non_trigger: Reuse evidence when its relevant envelope remains valid; explicit local reasoning may replace a dependency registry or global rerun.
trigger: A relevant environment, observer, tool/model, data distribution, dependency or obligation changes while earlier evidence is still being consumed.

bearer: Reachable joint states of independently considered edits, versions, mappings and responsibilities.
criterion: Newly reachable consequential combinations have adequate obligation evidence or are prevented; endpoint correctness is not silently extrapolated to the join.
name: Obligation continuity across reachable joint states
non_trigger: Proven disjointness, a genuine quiescent boundary or a simpler strategy can remove a combination; no exhaustive universal state model is required.
trigger: The selected composition creates materially new joint states or interactions not covered by its constituent endpoint evidence.

bearer: The combined maintenance-control arrangement and its continuing consumers, protection and total burden.
criterion: The selected combination has justified protection, consumers and continuation conditions; unnecessary controls can end while residual obligations remain protected.
name: Feedback-driven proportionality and retirement of combined controls
non_trigger: Use the existing adequate local method unchanged; a simple cost/consumer judgment can suffice without a meta-process or optimisation engine.
trigger: Several controls interact, compete for finite maintenance capacity or persist after their original obligations change.

bearer: The family consists of products whose shared domain assumptions warrant coordinated production; code resemblance alone is insufficient.
criterion: State which products and foreseeable needs belong together; test shared domain assumptions against counterexamples before committing to shared production.
name: Warranted family boundary
non_trigger: For incidental shared utilities, use ordinary component reuse or independent products without introducing a family programme.
trigger: A decision to coordinate assets or future variants across more than one product need.

bearer: The family consists of products whose shared domain assumptions warrant coordinated production; code resemblance alone is insufficient.
criterion: Compare requirements, products and expert explanations; separate invariant needs, intended variation and historical accidents; record disagreement rather than infer a common core from names.
name: Evidence of commonality and variability
non_trigger: A short reviewed comparison of a few stable products can replace an elaborate modelling exercise.
trigger: Establishing or revising the domain knowledge on which reusable assets depend.

bearer: The family consists of products whose shared domain assumptions warrant coordinated production; code resemblance alone is insufficient.
criterion: Admit a new variation only with a product or credible future need, an implementation boundary, an assurance consequence and an identified support cost.
name: Value-bound admission of variability
non_trigger: Keep a one-off requirement product-local, or postpone its generalisation until repeated demand supplies evidence.
trigger: A request to broaden the set of products or selectable behaviours.

bearer: Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.
criterion: Maintain a functional distinction between creating family capabilities and instantiating products, with explicit exchange of requirements, constraints and feasibility evidence.
name: Coupled domain and application responsibilities
non_trigger: The same people may perform both activities; a small family needs no separate departments or serial phases.
trigger: At least one asset or production decision is intended to serve several products.

bearer: Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.
criterion: Return a product observation with its configuration, asset baseline and consequence; decide whether to repair the core, adjust a constraint, retain an exception or revise scope.
name: Product-to-core feedback
non_trigger: A direct conversation and linked change record can suffice when the team and affected products are small.
trigger: Derivation failure, recurring local workaround, unexpected interaction or a justified new common need.

bearer: Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.
criterion: Permit a bounded product divergence with its baseline, purpose, support responsibility and conditions for reintegration or continued separation.
name: Product exceptions with retained lineage
non_trigger: A small isolated patch with a recorded origin may be better than a new family-wide variation point.
trigger: A product obligation cannot be met adequately through the current shared assets without disproportionate disruption.

bearer: Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.
criterion: Choose anticipatory domain investment, incremental extension or recovery from existing variants according to uncertainty, existing assets and available migration capacity.
name: Selection among proactive, reactive and extractive adoption
non_trigger: Reuse a few stable assets or retain clone-and-own while collecting evidence; no immediate platform conversion is required.
trigger: Starting a product line or changing how an existing portfolio is produced.

bearer: The model represents a declared product family, not every conceivable configuration in the technology domain.
criterion: Define what each feature denotes, who interprets it and how selections relate to requirements, implementation and runtime capability.
name: Explicit feature semantics
non_trigger: A compact glossary plus explicit configuration rules can be sufficient; a tree is optional.
trigger: Features are used to negotiate products, derive artefacts or justify assurance.

bearer: The model represents a declared product family, not every conceivable configuration in the technology domain.
criterion: Check the model's declared semantics for consistency and investigate diagnoses relative to intended configurations; report the exact model and solver interpretation.
name: Constraint-consistency diagnostics
non_trigger: Exhaustive enumeration or a manually checked decision table may suffice for a tiny model.
trigger: Constraints are nontrivial, edited, combined or used to reject user selections.

bearer: The model represents a declared product family, not every conceivable configuration in the technology domain.
criterion: Validate constraints against representative positive and negative product scenarios, expert knowledge and implementation evidence; explicitly record unmodelled conditions.
name: Validation of domain-constraint adequacy
non_trigger: Review a small set of known supported and forbidden combinations instead of building a comprehensive formal ontology.
trigger: A variability model is relied upon to accept or exclude product choices.

bearer: The model represents a declared product family, not every conceivable configuration in the technology domain.
criterion: Relate a conflict or forced choice to the smallest useful set of decisions and constraints; permit human correction and show relevant provenance.
name: Explanation-assisted configuration
non_trigger: A domain expert can explain a small stable set of rules directly; automated minimal explanations are not always needed.
trigger: Configuration choices are numerous, cross-constrained or made by users without implementation expertise.

bearer: The model represents a declared product family, not every conceivable configuration in the technology domain.
criterion: Use the least expressive representation that preserves required distinctions; verify translations and tool support for the actual language level.
name: Richer variability types when the domain requires them
non_trigger: Keep a Boolean model or a small typed table when that already captures consequential decisions.
trigger: The domain requires multiplicity, arithmetic, typed values or constraints not expressible adequately by simple selection.

bearer: Realisation choices serve the selected family scope rather than requiring all products to share one implementation technique.
criterion: Choose a binding time for each variation by weighing when information becomes available against footprint, assurance, deployment and runtime transition costs.
name: Deliberate binding-time selection
non_trigger: Bind early when the required choice is already known and later change has no justified value.
trigger: A variation point is introduced or its resolution time changes.

bearer: Realisation choices serve the selected family scope rather than requiring all products to share one implementation technique.
criterion: Preserve the feature-to-artefact relations needed for derivation, change impact and diagnosis, including build selection, generator input and shared implementation.
name: Feature-to-realisation traceability
non_trigger: Local naming, module structure and a small checked mapping can replace a comprehensive trace database.
trigger: Consequential changes or product construction depend on understanding how a feature is realised.

bearer: Realisation choices serve the selected family scope rather than requiring all products to share one implementation technique.
criterion: Select among conditional code, parameters, component/plugin substitution, inheritance, aspects, feature modules and transformations according to local constraints; explicitly manage cross-mechanism interactions.
name: A portfolio of variability realisation techniques
non_trigger: Retain an ordinary parameter or small conditional when it is understandable and adequately checked.
trigger: Designing or restructuring the realisation of family variation.

bearer: Realisation choices serve the selected family scope rather than requiring all products to share one implementation technique.
criterion: Define applicable deltas, their dependencies or order and the validity conditions of each modification; verify the resulting product rather than assuming arbitrary edits commute.
name: Ordered and conditional delta composition
non_trigger: Use direct modules or parameters where no meaningful transformation sequence is needed.
trigger: Product differences naturally require structured additions, removals or changes over a shared base.

bearer: Realisation choices serve the selected family scope rather than requiring all products to share one implementation technique.
criterion: Validate the mapping from selections and asset versions to generated structure and behaviour, using applicable checks on transformations and produced products.
name: Validation of generator realisation
non_trigger: Review a simple deterministic template and test representative outputs; do not require a universal proof of the generator.
trigger: Product derivation relies on generation or nontrivial transformation of shared assets.

bearer: Core assets and production plans are bounded by the supported family and its product obligations.
criterion: Treat non-code work products as reusable assets where products actually consume them, with compatible versioning and variation information.
name: Reusable non-code assets with consumers
non_trigger: Share only the few requirements, tests or instructions that have a real consumer; a full document suite is not obligatory.
trigger: Repeated product work depends on shared engineering knowledge beyond implementation code.

bearer: Core assets and production plans are bounded by the supported family and its product obligations.
criterion: State the architectural invariants required for reuse and the permitted substitutions; enforce or check them in the derivation path where the claim requires enforcement.
name: Family architectural invariants and variation boundaries
non_trigger: A few stable interfaces and reviewed component choices can suffice; an elaborate reference architecture is unnecessary for a small family.
trigger: Shared components, interfaces or assurance depend on product architecture remaining within a known class.

bearer: Core assets and production plans are bounded by the supported family and its product obligations.
criterion: Maintain an actionable, version-related derivation procedure that tells builders which decisions, assets, tools and checks produce a supported product.
name: A versioned product-derivation plan
non_trigger: A short script plus explicit human decisions can be a complete plan for a small stable family.
trigger: Products must be reproduced, handed to another team or built repeatedly from shared assets.

bearer: Core assets and production plans are bounded by the supported family and its product obligations.
criterion: Identify the configuration and the relevant asset, generator, dependency and tool versions together; distinguish requested configuration from realised product identity.
name: Configuration, asset and tool baseline identity
non_trigger: A versioned configuration file and pinned build inputs may suffice; a new provenance service is not inherently required.
trigger: Reproduction, support, change impact or transfer of an assurance result depends on knowing what was built.

bearer: Core assets and production plans are bounded by the supported family and its product obligations.
criterion: Declare whether repeatability means equal feature realisation, equivalent tested behaviour, identical generated source or identical bytes, then control the inputs necessary for that claim.
name: Repeatable derivation at a declared equivalence level
non_trigger: Behavioural or structural equivalence may be adequate; do not impose bit-for-bit output where timestamps or tool differences are immaterial.
trigger: Support, certification, comparison or distribution requires reliable reconstruction of a product.

bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
criterion: State each assurance claim's object, quantified configurations, inputs, environment and baseline; identify the realisation obligations needed to carry it to a product.
name: Layer-specific assurance claims
non_trigger: A concise claim-and-boundary statement attached to the result can be sufficient.
trigger: A model, test, proof or analysis result is used to justify a product or family decision.

bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
criterion: Identify plausible interaction mechanisms and select checks whose coverage matches their order and risk; include shared-asset and environmental interactions, not only adjacent feature-tree nodes.
name: Interaction-aware coverage
non_trigger: Isolated independent substitutions may need only interface checks; do not impose high-order combinatorial testing without an interaction rationale.
trigger: Features share state, resources, protocols, build choices or behavioural assumptions.

bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
criterion: Sample valid configurations using a declared objective and budget, include critical known combinations, and report residual higher-order or environmental coverage limits.
name: Constrained and risk-informed sampling
non_trigger: Test every supported configuration when the family is small, or analyse a relevant shared property once when a sound family analysis is cheaper.
trigger: Full enumeration is infeasible and a bounded sample can provide useful assurance.

bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
criterion: Preserve variation symbolically or structurally during analysis so common computations are reused, while retaining conditions under which each result applies.
name: Family-based sharing of analysis
non_trigger: Ordinary product analysis is preferable for a few configurations or unsupported languages and artefacts.
trigger: Many products share analyzable structure and the analysis implementation supports their variability semantics.

bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
criterion: State the assumptions and guarantees of a feature or component and discharge compatibility and interaction obligations when composing selected parts.
name: Compositional feature contracts
non_trigger: Check the whole derived product when contracts would be harder to specify or maintain than the verification itself.
trigger: Stable interfaces and separable properties make local reasoning reusable across products.

bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
criterion: Check the actual derived artefacts against the selected product obligations and operating context, reusing family evidence only where its premises apply.
name: Acceptance of the actual derived product
non_trigger: Reuse valid existing evidence and perform only the additional product checks needed for unestablished obligations; repeated full testing is not automatically required.
trigger: A product is delivered, deployed or materially changed.

bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
criterion: Include the configuration layers relevant to the claimed result and track approximation or unsupported constructs in the extraction chain.
name: Analysis of build, macro and configuration layers
non_trigger: A single checked configuration layer is enough when the derivation genuinely has no hidden variation elsewhere.
trigger: Build, dependency or generator configuration affects product realisation or static-analysis reach.

bearer: Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.
criterion: Compare old and new model semantics using an explicit feature correspondence; classify preserved, added and removed configurations before selecting migration or regression work.
name: Semantic classification of feature-model edits
non_trigger: Enumerate and compare all configurations for a small family rather than introduce a specialised solver.
trigger: A feature model, cross-tree constraint or feature vocabulary changes.

bearer: Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.
criterion: Map old selections and product intent to a permitted new configuration, accounting for intermediate constraints, change costs and the actual resulting product.
name: Intent-preserving configuration migration
non_trigger: Retain a supported older baseline or use a reviewed manual migration when the portfolio is small.
trigger: A supported product must move to a changed model, core baseline or production environment.

bearer: Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.
criterion: Identify affected products and assumptions, select appropriate regression evidence and coordinate propagation, exceptions or supported parallel versions.
name: Impact and regression analysis of shared changes
non_trigger: Use local regression when the changed asset is demonstrably product-local; reuse established evidence for unaffected products.
trigger: A shared requirement, component, test, model or production tool changes materially.

bearer: Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.
criterion: State compatible baseline combinations and supported release relationships; allow coordinated or independent product schedules while making upgrade and support obligations explicit.
name: Supported baseline and release relationships
non_trigger: A single synchronised release may be adequate when all products and stakeholders can genuinely move together.
trigger: Products, core assets or tools evolve on different schedules.

bearer: Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.
criterion: Recover candidate features and constraints from multiple artefact types, preserve existing valid domain knowledge and review recovered relations against product intent.
name: Recovery of variability with domain reconciliation
non_trigger: Compare a few existing products manually; do not introduce a general extraction framework for a tiny stable portfolio.
trigger: Consolidating variants, repairing stale models or reducing dependence on tacit configuration knowledge.

bearer: Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.
criterion: Reassess test-configuration validity and purpose after model change; choose repair, fresh generation or targeted new-product tests according to regression and novelty objectives.
name: Co-evolution of configuration-oriented tests
non_trigger: Retain still-valid tests and manually add a few relevant configurations when changes are small.
trigger: A feature-model change alters permitted products or test-selection assumptions.

bearer: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
criterion: Compare lifecycle costs and required outcomes over an explicit horizon; vary demand, reuse rate and maintenance assumptions rather than rely on a universal break-even count.
name: Lifecycle economics with uncertainty
non_trigger: Use a coarse scenario comparison when precise estimates are not credible; keep assumptions visible rather than manufacture precision.
trigger: An investment or continuation decision depends on product-line benefits.

bearer: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
criterion: Compare SPLE with clone-and-own, selective component reuse, a modular single product or independent development under the same quality and support obligations.
name: An explicit adequate non-product-line alternative
non_trigger: Keep the adequate non-product-line method when its total burden is lower or the product-line benefit is not established.
trigger: Choosing or defending shared family production.

bearer: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
criterion: Reassess future costs and obligations at material changes; narrow, split, retire or continue the family based on prospective adequacy, preserving outstanding support.
name: Economic reassessment without a sunk-cost veto
non_trigger: A brief decision review using actual product experience may replace a recurrent formal business-case ceremony.
trigger: Demand changes, reuse disappoints, coordination dominates or the product portfolio contracts.

bearer: Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.
criterion: Make contribution, variation and release decision rights explicit; provide a proportionate way to adjudicate competing product obligations and fund accepted shared work.
name: Authority and arbitration for shared assets
non_trigger: A named maintainer and direct product-owner agreement can suffice; a new committee is not a property.
trigger: Shared changes affect products with different priorities or authorities.

bearer: Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.
criterion: Align skills, capacity, incentives and cost allocation with the intended shared-production responsibilities; scale commitments to actual capability.
name: Capability, incentives and resource alignment
non_trigger: Start with a limited shared capability and existing staff rather than create a full platform organisation before demand is known.
trigger: A product-line plan requires work or coordination beyond the existing organisation's supported practice.

bearer: Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.
criterion: Identify who controls assets, proposals, interfaces and releases; distinguish contractual or negotiated compatibility from internal derivation authority; export bounded interfaces rather than fictitious central control.
name: An explicit ecosystem participation boundary
non_trigger: Manage a bounded component dependency when no broader ecosystem coordination is required.
trigger: Suppliers, open-source participants or independent platform users determine material variation.

bearer: Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.
criterion: Associate externally supplied obligations with affected assets and products, then require appropriate evidence or specialist adjudication before deriving or changing those products.
name: Traceability of externally specified obligations
non_trigger: Preserve the relevant external requirement and its affected products; do not invent a new compliance framework or a legal conclusion.
trigger: Supplier conditions, security requirements, licences, regulation or support commitments constrain valid product use.

bearer: Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.
criterion: Model permitted runtime configurations, relevant context and the mapping from observations to proposed reconfiguration; connect the decision to actual actuators and feedback.
name: Context-to-configuration mapping for dynamic families
non_trigger: Select a static or deployment-time variant when runtime rebinding is not required.
trigger: A product must change its selected capabilities during execution as conditions change.

bearer: Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.
criterion: Check the transition path, quiescence or state transfer and actual controllability; preserve safety requirements throughout the operating phase or enter a separately justified safe reconfiguration phase.
name: Transition safety and state continuity
non_trigger: Stop and restart in a known safe condition, or prohibit runtime switching, when live transition assurance is disproportionate.
trigger: Features or components are rebound while the system is operating.

bearer: Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.
criterion: Synthesize a supervisor for the modelled plant and requirements, then establish that observations, event controllability and actuation match the implementation.
name: Supervisory control under plant assumptions
non_trigger: A reviewed transition table or offline configuration can suffice where synthesis adds no justified assurance.
trigger: A finite-state or otherwise supported discrete-event model adequately captures a consequential dynamic product-line problem.

bearer: Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.
criterion: Specify the supported language level and check semantic preservation for translations and toolchains; make unsupported constructs explicit.
name: Semantic fidelity in variability interchange
non_trigger: Keep one stable representation and tool when interchange has no real consumer.
trigger: Variability models move across tools, organisations or analysis backends.

bearer: Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.
criterion: Treat generated changes as proposals; validate syntax, constraints, semantic intent, realisation and product obligations using appropriate independent checks before acceptance.
name: AI-assisted migration as a validated proposal
non_trigger: Use deterministic constraint solving, a conventional transformation or manual review when these are cheaper and adequate.
trigger: Learned tools assist feature modelling, configuration advice, migration or variant generation.

bearer: Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.
criterion: The candidate is a replacement strategy: retain specifications and regenerate variants. Its stronger claim of superior lifecycle adequacy is not established by the inspected evidence.
name: LLM regeneration as a superior replacement for maintained variability
non_trigger: Keep maintained assets and use an assistant only for bounded changes; conventional generation remains an alternative.
trigger: Considering regeneration as a substitute for a maintained family realisation, not merely as assistance.

bearer: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
criterion: No general mechanism supports the universal threshold. Replace the claim with a horizon-specific comparison of investment, derivation, coordination and support costs.
name: A universal break-even product count
non_trigger: A small scenario calculation showing the relevant cost drivers is adequate to reject the fixed threshold.
trigger: A proposed adoption is justified by reaching a supposedly universal number of products.

bearer: Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.
criterion: Reject the universal prerequisite; use the proactive, reactive, extractive or hybrid route justified by the actual starting conditions.
name: A complete upfront platform as a prerequisite
non_trigger: Start with a bounded common asset and one product, then expand only when evidence warrants it.
trigger: A process requires complete domain assets before permitting useful product work.

bearer: The model represents a declared product family, not every conceivable configuration in the technology domain.
criterion: Reject artefact sufficiency; require meaningful features, usable constraints, a relation to realisation and an actual configuration or change consumer.
name: A feature-tree artefact as sufficient variability management
non_trigger: A checked decision table or direct configuration rules may supply the required function without a tree.
trigger: A diagram, modelling tool or documentation checklist is offered as the evidence of control.

bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
criterion: Reject the implication. Keep model consistency, realisation correctness and product behaviour as separate claims with explicit connecting premises.
name: Feature-model satisfiability as delivered-product correctness
non_trigger: Show a concrete missing domain constraint or faulty realisation to expose the gap; retain the SAT check for its genuine purpose.
trigger: A SAT result is used to assert product correctness or release readiness.

bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
criterion: Reject the guarantee; use pairwise testing only as a bounded selection strategy within an explicit assurance argument.
name: Pairwise coverage as family correctness
non_trigger: A four-row three-feature counterexample demonstrates the logical gap without a large experiment.
trigger: A pairwise coverage percentage is presented as complete family assurance.

bearer: Realisation choices serve the selected family scope rather than requiring all products to share one implementation technique.
criterion: Reject a universal ranking and select binding time by the timing of needed knowledge and the costs of retained flexibility.
name: Later binding as universally better
non_trigger: Fix the choice earlier and rebuild or redeploy when rare changes occur.
trigger: A compile/deployment-time choice is moved later without a concrete operational need.

bearer: Realisation choices serve the selected family scope rather than requiring all products to share one implementation technique.
criterion: Reject the universal correspondence; model the relations needed for derivation and impact, allowing many-to-many mappings and interaction artefacts.
name: A universal one-feature/one-module correspondence
non_trigger: Keep a simple mapping where it genuinely exists; do not introduce complexity solely to avoid one-to-one cases.
trigger: Traceability or architecture forces a one-to-one feature/module decomposition.

bearer: Core assets and production plans are bounded by the supported family and its product obligations.
criterion: Reject total automation as a universal definition; require a defined, adequate derivation method and evidence for the resulting products.
name: Total automation as the definition of SPLE
non_trigger: A reliable reviewed manual derivation can be sufficient for a small stable family.
trigger: Automation percentage is used as the criterion for product-line existence or maturity.

bearer: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
criterion: Reject universal inadmissibility; compare cloning's immediate adequacy and future synchronisation costs with the actual product-line alternative.
name: Clone-and-own as universally inadmissible
non_trigger: Retain clones with sufficient provenance and targeted shared-fix tracking when they are the lower-cost adequate solution.
trigger: Cloning is rejected without examining portfolio conditions or maintenance obligations.

bearer: Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.
criterion: Reject the equivalence; preserve or explicitly change feature intent and verify the actual migrated product's obligations.
name: Stable names or configuration sets as behavioural compatibility
non_trigger: A targeted behavioural regression can be sufficient where a full migration analysis adds nothing.
trigger: Compatibility is asserted solely because names or model-level product sets did not change.

bearer: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
criterion: Use counts to estimate analysis, support or selection complexity; assess value through useful products and avoided costs rather than raw combinatorics.
name: Raw configuration count as a benefit measure
non_trigger: Count supported or demanded products and their costs when theoretical possibilities do not affect the decision.
trigger: Configuration-space size is used in an investment or maturity claim.

bearer: Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.
criterion: Reject self-authorising control; separately establish observation, actual actuation capability, external permission and the expected consequence.
name: Formal modelling as operational authority
non_trigger: Keep the result advisory or use an existing authorised operational process when actuation is not established.
trigger: A formal or generated controller is proposed for real runtime configuration.

bearer: Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.
criterion: Distinguish admission to new products from continued support of existing ones; retire or bind variability when its consumer disappears, preserving required historical baselines and migration paths.
name: Support-aware retirement of variability
non_trigger: Mark the feature unavailable to new configurations while retaining the older baseline, rather than immediately rewriting all code.
trigger: A feature is unused for new demand, fixed to one value or becomes disproportionately costly to support.

bearer: Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.
criterion: Reject that stronger implication. Retain the narrower distinction that selected features are fixed after a declared binding time; analyse inputs, state, timing and environment separately.
name: Null configurability as context-independent behaviour
non_trigger: A fixed-function program that reads a changing external value supplies a logical counterexample to the stronger inference.
trigger: Fixed feature selection is used to infer environment-independent behaviour or a general correctness guarantee.

bearer: Process purposes, beneficiaries and strategic outcome commitments
criterion: A proposed change can be judged against an explicit outcome and identified recipients, rather than only a department’s activity count.
name: End-to-end purposes and beneficiaries
non_trigger: For a small, already understood service, a short agreed purpose and completion statement plus sample cases is sufficient; no portfolio exercise is required.
trigger: A process is being selected, assessed or changed and local success may differ from the received outcome.

bearer: Outcome/improvement claims over an affected-party consequence boundary
criterion: An apparent local gain is accepted, qualified or rejected with its downstream and affected-person consequences visible.
name: Boundary accountability and displaced burdens
non_trigger: Inspect a few complete cases and ask receiving participants what changed. A full network model is unnecessary when interfaces and effects are simple.
trigger: A local measure improves, work is outsourced, or a redesigned interface changes another actor’s burden.

bearer: Process cases, triggering needs and continuing/completion responsibilities
criterion: Cases used in measures or routing have a stated identity rule, with ambiguous or continuing cases identified.
name: Identifiable cases, triggers and completion
non_trigger: Use a lightweight episode or work-object account; where no stable repeated structure exists, coordinate goals and obligations without heavy process standardisation.
trigger: Measurement, discovery or enactment depends on assigning work to cases and deciding whether work is finished.

bearer: Intervention portfolio and chosen scale of change
criterion: Chosen and omitted interventions have intelligible reasons tied to expected consequences and capacity.
name: Selective process portfolio intervention
non_trigger: A direct, well-evidenced local repair can proceed without constructing an organisation-wide portfolio.
trigger: Several process problems compete for limited analytical or change resources.

bearer: Process architecture and cross-process dependencies
criterion: An analyst can locate the affected process and its consequential relationships without equating reporting lines with work flow.
name: Process architecture with preserved dependencies
non_trigger: For a small scope, an interface list with responsible participants can replace a full architecture hierarchy.
trigger: Several processes share resources, objects or interfaces and local changes can conflict.

bearer: Accounts of performed work, variants and observations outside current models
criterion: The as-is account identifies its sources, covered variants and consequential uncertainties.
name: Triangulated discovery of performed work
non_trigger: For a transparent low-risk process, a few representative walkthroughs with performers and recipients may suffice; all evidence channels are not compulsory.
trigger: A decision depends on what actually happens and available accounts may be incomplete, selective or incentive-distorted.

bearer: Participant validation, learning and consequential participation arrangements
criterion: Users can apply the representation to the relevant case distinction, or a specific unresolved disagreement is recorded.
name: Participant validation and explicit disagreement
non_trigger: A brief case walkthrough or annotated narrative may establish the needed understanding without a workshop series.
trigger: A process model or redesign will be used across roles with different knowledge or incentives.

bearer: Accounts of performed work, variants and observations outside current models
criterion: A redesign claim states the case classes it covers and the exceptions that could defeat it.
name: Variant and exception coverage in discovery
non_trigger: Use a few deliberately contrasting cases when the variant space is small; exhaustive enumeration is unnecessary.
trigger: Case mix, exceptions or hidden handoffs could change analysis or redesign conclusions.

bearer: Event/shared-data interpretation and its relationship to actual work
criterion: Claims derived from logs specify what was recorded, transformed and excluded, including consequential blind spots.
name: Event-data provenance and observability limits
non_trigger: A small manually checked sample and extraction description may be sufficient; a mining platform is not required.
trigger: Event data will justify an as-is claim, comparison, forecast or intervention.

bearer: Process representations and the distinctions/quality claims supported by them
criterion: The consumer can make the intended distinction, and prohibited or unsupported uses are visible.
name: Purpose-fit representation and abstraction
non_trigger: Use the lightest already-understood representation that preserves the needed distinction; no diagram is required where a short narrative is enough.
trigger: A representation is being selected, simplified, shared or reused for a new purpose.

bearer: Process representations and the distinctions/quality claims supported by them
criterion: A model’s validation statement says which quality dimensions were tested and what remains unestablished.
name: Separate syntactic, semantic and pragmatic quality
non_trigger: A short review against examples may suffice for a simple narrative; formal syntax checks apply only to notations that have such rules.
trigger: A model will justify a decision, communicate consequential instructions or support execution.

bearer: Process representations and the distinctions/quality claims supported by them
criterion: Users handle the relevant cases at least adequately without loss of critical constraints or relationships.
name: Behaviour-preserving complexity management
non_trigger: Remove an ambiguity or improve a label before imposing a new modelling standard or decomposition programme.
trigger: Users cannot reliably interpret a model, or model changes introduce structural errors.

bearer: Process representations and the distinctions/quality claims supported by them
criterion: Critical labels support the intended action/object distinction across the relevant users.
name: Interpretable activity labels and domain terms
non_trigger: A brief glossary or example can be enough; a mandatory naming convention is unnecessary when existing terms work.
trigger: Users disagree about an activity, decision or completion label, or labels are reused across roles.

bearer: The modelling-versus-execution contract between a process representation, enactment and actual work
criterion: The model’s claimed scope matches tested implementation behaviour and does not silently certify organisational consequences.
name: Explicit modelling-versus-execution contract
non_trigger: For a descriptive model, simply state that it is not executable; do not build an execution contract unnecessarily.
trigger: A model is handed to implementers, imported into a tool or presented as evidence that a process operates correctly.

bearer: Decision rules, their consumers and separately authorised decision-makers
criterion: A decision can be explained and changed without silently changing who may make it or what outcome follows.
name: Separable decision logic and decision authority
non_trigger: A decision table or explicit rationale can be sufficient; DMN is an option rather than an obligation.
trigger: Business decisions are obscured in flow diagrams, reused across processes or changed independently of task order.

bearer: Knowledge-work support, discretion, variants and binding constraints
criterion: Participants can adapt the work while preserving essential obligations and keeping others informed.
name: Knowledge-work and declarative alternatives
non_trigger: A shared case note, goal list and essential constraints can be enough without a case-management engine.
trigger: Cases require changing knowledge, professional judgement or runtime planning that an exhaustive flow would distort.

bearer: Outcome/improvement claims over an affected-party consequence boundary
criterion: An improvement claim states which outcomes changed, which worsened and whose experience is represented.
name: Outcome-valid, plural performance measures
non_trigger: A small set of outcome and harm checks can be sufficient; a comprehensive balanced dashboard is not mandatory.
trigger: Measures will guide resource allocation, redesign acceptance or individual/process appraisal.

bearer: Elapsed process time, effort and resource occupancy claims
criterion: A delay claim no longer conflates a worker’s effort with the case’s elapsed duration.
name: Elapsed time distinguished from work effort
non_trigger: A manually reconstructed case timeline can be adequate; detailed time logging is unnecessary when the causal bottleneck is already clear.
trigger: A time-based performance claim or delay intervention is being made.

bearer: Capacity/queueing/simulation model and conditional intervention predictions
criterion: The selected intervention targets a supported constraint and includes evidence about the resulting queue and displaced load.
name: Capacity, variability and bottleneck diagnosis
non_trigger: A workload/timeline comparison and a bounded allocation trial may dominate building a detailed stochastic model.
trigger: Persistent queues, fluctuating demand or shared-resource contention dominate outcomes.

bearer: Handoff and rework mechanisms, including necessary repair/checking
criterion: A claimed rework reduction is tied to a changed causal mechanism and retained necessary controls.
name: Handoff and rework mechanism diagnosis
non_trigger: Walk a few failed cases and repair a single information or responsibility defect before redesigning the entire process.
trigger: Cases bounce between actors, repeatedly request information or suffer unexplained rejection/delay.

bearer: Capacity/queueing/simulation model and conditional intervention predictions
criterion: A simulation-supported choice includes an empirical calibration check and conditions under which the prediction is not relied upon.
name: Calibrated simulation with uncertainty
non_trigger: Use arithmetic, a case timeline or a limited real-world trial when these answer the decision adequately.
trigger: Alternatives are costly or disruptive to test directly, or queues/current cases make short-term effects non-obvious.

bearer: Intervention hypotheses, comparisons and analytical claim roles
criterion: The decision states whether evidence is descriptive, predictive or causally identifying, with material alternative explanations visible.
name: Causal restraint in intervention selection
non_trigger: A modest reversible trial with explicit observations can be more informative than a complex causal model based on weak assumptions.
trigger: A variant, actor or activity is blamed for an outcome, or a predicted association is used to choose a change.

bearer: Intervention hypotheses, comparisons and analytical claim roles
criterion: A selected redesign has an explicit mechanism, comparison and evaluable consequences rather than a technology-first justification.
name: Hypothesis-led comparison of redesign alternatives
non_trigger: A small reversible change with a simple comparison may be enough; no full redesign workshop or simulation is necessary.
trigger: A process intervention is proposed and multiple mechanisms could address the problem.

bearer: Tasks/controls proposed for removal and their protected functions
criterion: The removed task’s necessary functions are either explicitly retired with reasons or demonstrably covered elsewhere.
name: Control-aware task elimination
non_trigger: Retain a cheap effective check when redesign cost or uncertain risk exceeds its burden; combine duplicate checks only after their distinct functions are understood.
trigger: A step is labelled waste, redundant approval or avoidable checking.

bearer: Task order and information/resource/commitment dependencies
criterion: The revised order avoids targeted delay or unnecessary work without invalidating required inputs or controls.
name: Dependency-aware resequencing
non_trigger: Keep the current order when dependencies are tight or savings are negligible; try a small reversible ordering change first.
trigger: Cases commonly fail late or an ordering constraint appears unnecessary.

bearer: Concurrent activities, joins and resulting partial effects
criterion: Elapsed time improves without unaccounted duplicate work, incompatible outputs or stranded partial completion.
name: Synchronisation-aware parallelisation
non_trigger: Keep serial execution when coordination or rework dominates; overlap only the independent portion.
trigger: Serial waiting dominates and dependencies permit overlapping work.

bearer: Case coordination, allocation, pooling and segmentation arrangements
criterion: Case continuity improves while required specialist/control functions remain effective.
name: Case coordination and task composition
non_trigger: A shared case note and named coordinator can be enough; do not require one person to perform every specialist task.
trigger: Cases repeatedly lose context or stall between fragmented responsibilities.

bearer: Case coordination, allocation, pooling and segmentation arrangements
criterion: Pooling produces a defensible overall result, including access and delay for small or exceptional groups.
name: Conditional pooling and centralisation
non_trigger: Retain local provision when responsiveness, contextual expertise or failure isolation dominates.
trigger: Duplicated capabilities or uneven demand suggest a pooling opportunity.

bearer: Case coordination, allocation, pooling and segmentation arrangements
criterion: Case groups receive fit-for-purpose handling with visible misclassification and unequal-service effects.
name: Case segmentation and skill allocation
non_trigger: Keep one route with an exception option when classification adds more error or delay than it removes.
trigger: A common route performs poorly for distinct needs, risks or required expertise.

bearer: Intervention portfolio and chosen scale of change
criterion: The chosen change scale matches the problem and includes credible continuity and evaluation arrangements.
name: Proportionate radical or incremental change
non_trigger: Retain or repair a functioning process when disruption has no warranted payoff.
trigger: The current process is being reconsidered or incremental changes repeatedly fail to address a structural problem.

bearer: Process governance arrangements and exercised authority
criterion: A consequential cross-functional decision can actually be made and implemented by identified actors.
name: Process ownership with effective authority
non_trigger: In a small team, existing management and a clear escalation agreement may suffice; no extra role is required.
trigger: An end-to-end problem crosses functional authority or an owner is assigned responsibility.

bearer: Process purposes, beneficiaries and strategic outcome commitments
criterion: Investment and redesign choices have a traceable substantive reason and can be challenged when consequences contradict it.
name: Strategy-to-process translation
non_trigger: A small service can use a few agreed outcome priorities without a formal strategy cascade.
trigger: Processes compete for investment or strategic objectives change.

bearer: Process governance arrangements and exercised authority
criterion: The chosen arrangement resolves identified coordination needs without unexplained duplication or authority gaps.
name: Context-fit BPM governance configuration
non_trigger: Use existing management and a few explicit coordination agreements when they resolve the actual decisions.
trigger: Multiple units need coordination, common methods or shared process investment.

bearer: Capability/maturity assessments and claims made from their artefacts or ratings
criterion: Assessment produces testable development priorities or an explicit decision that no further machinery is warranted.
name: Capability assessment as fallible diagnosis
non_trigger: Investigate the actual failed decisions or processes directly when a broad assessment would not change action.
trigger: An organisation needs to diagnose capability gaps or choose improvement support.

bearer: Participant validation, learning and consequential participation arrangements
criterion: Relevant knowledge changes the design or is explicitly adjudicated, and actors can perform the new work.
name: Participation, learning and incentive alignment
non_trigger: Direct discussion and guided practice may suffice for a small change; a formal change programme is not always needed.
trigger: A change depends on new behaviour, tacit knowledge or acceptance by affected actors.

bearer: Knowledge-work support, discretion, variants and binding constraints
criterion: The case can proceed or stop for defensible reasons without losing necessary accountability.
name: Bounded human discretion and exceptions
non_trigger: For low-risk, simple work, a clear goal and accessible expert may suffice without a case-management platform.
trigger: Case facts invalidate the normal route or expertise is needed beyond a fixed activity sequence.

bearer: A workaround and its cause, purpose, risks and authorised disposition
criterion: The workaround receives an evidence-based disposition and material unresolved consequences are visible.
name: Workaround-driven misalignment inquiry
non_trigger: Resolve an isolated, understood mismatch locally when no wider change is justified.
trigger: Actors repeatedly bypass a prescribed procedure or information system.

bearer: Process visibility, appraisal, incentives and affected-person protection
criterion: The evidence used for decisions has a defensible purpose and access boundary, with harms and disputes visible.
name: Responsible visibility and affected-person protection
non_trigger: Use aggregate, sampled or less identifying evidence when it answers the decision adequately; omit monitoring with no legitimate consumer.
trigger: Monitoring, employee-level data, sensitive case information or consequential algorithmic decisions are introduced.

bearer: Process visibility, appraisal, incentives and affected-person protection
criterion: An appraisal or improvement decision accounts for known distortions and does not equate target attainment with the entire outcome.
name: Incentive-aware appraisal and metric interpretation
non_trigger: Use qualitative review or aggregate learning measures where precise individual attribution is not warranted.
trigger: A measure affects pay, ranking, sanctions, targets or resource access.

bearer: Socio-technical enactment, automation or low-code delivery and actual received consequences
criterion: Real cases are completed under the new arrangement with responsibilities and observed consequences understood.
name: Socio-technical enactment and adoption
non_trigger: An organisational agreement, training or information change may suffice without new software.
trigger: A to-be design is introduced or a new system is claimed to improve a process.

bearer: Socio-technical enactment, automation or low-code delivery and actual received consequences
criterion: The selected mechanism performs its bounded function under stated conditions, with business consequences evaluated separately.
name: Selective automation and interface suitability
non_trigger: Retain manual work or improve information/organisation when exception cost or integration fragility outweighs automation benefit.
trigger: Repetitive digital work or coordination overhead suggests a technical intervention.

bearer: Business/external obligation completion and receiving-side evidence
criterion: Declared completion corresponds to the agreed business outcome, or remaining uncertainty and responsibility are explicit.
name: External-effect and completion reconciliation
non_trigger: A direct recipient confirmation or simple reconciliation may suffice; do not require a new distributed protocol for every process.
trigger: A process sends messages, transfers goods or money, changes external records or closes an obligation.

bearer: Interrupted work, outstanding obligations and authorised continuation/recovery
criterion: An interrupted case is not silently treated as completed, and an accountable decision governs continuation or resolution.
name: Recovery and controlled interruption
non_trigger: For a reversible low-impact task, manual stop-and-check with a responsible person may be sufficient.
trigger: Work can fail after consequential action or unsafe continuation is plausible.

bearer: Monitoring outputs linked, or not linked, to a capable decision consumer
criterion: A relevant observation results in a documented decision, inquiry or reasoned non-action rather than passive reporting.
name: Decision-linked monitoring
non_trigger: Periodic case review or a simple threshold with a known responder may suffice; retire indicators with no current decision use.
trigger: Process measures or monitoring are introduced or reviewed.

bearer: Changed demand, models, practice and assumptions requiring reassessment
criterion: The change is classified and consequential assumptions or controls are reviewed with reasons.
name: Drift-sensitive reassessment
non_trigger: A focused review of changed cases may suffice; continuous automated drift detection is unnecessary for infrequent stable work.
trigger: Observed patterns differ materially from the baseline or the operating environment changes.

bearer: Post-enactment outcome evaluation and control continuation/retirement decision
criterion: The change receives a reasoned retain, revise, withdraw or evidence-insufficient decision.
name: Outcome evaluation and control retirement
non_trigger: A small before/after case review may support a reversible local decision, with causal limits stated; no new intervention is an acceptable result.
trigger: A change has been enacted, an evaluation point arrives, or a control’s continued value is questioned.

bearer: Accounts of performed work, variants and observations outside current models
criterion: A material discrepancy can lead to changed inquiry or explicit adjudication rather than exclusion as out of scope by definition.
name: Feedback that can expose omitted work
non_trigger: Occasional independent case walkthroughs and accessible complaint routes may suffice; exhaustive surveillance is not required.
trigger: A process is evaluated primarily through records generated by its existing model or system.

bearer: Negotiated cross-organisational obligations and dispute/decision rights
criterion: A cross-organisational issue has an agreed decision route and responsibilities visible to participating parties.
name: Negotiated inter-organisational governance
non_trigger: A clear bilateral interface and escalation agreement may suffice for a simple relationship.
trigger: A received outcome depends on independent organisations with their own commitments.

bearer: Event/shared-data interpretation and its relationship to actual work
criterion: A receiving actor can interpret the shared evidence for the intended decision, with missing or incompatible meaning explicit.
name: Shared-data meaning and disclosure boundaries
non_trigger: Agree a small set of shared terms and examples when broad semantic standardisation would add no value.
trigger: Data or messages cross organisational/system boundaries or are joined for analysis.

bearer: Outcome/improvement claims over an affected-party consequence boundary
criterion: A sustainability claim states what changed, for whom, over which boundary and with what evidence limits.
name: Environmental and societal outcome constraints
non_trigger: A focused material-impact assessment may suffice; do not add an ESG dashboard unrelated to a consequential decision.
trigger: A process has material resource, environmental or social consequences or a sponsor claims sustainable improvement.

bearer: Intervention hypotheses, comparisons and analytical claim roles
criterion: An analytical result is accepted only for a stated evidential role and its action/outcome claims are separately evaluated.
name: Process intelligence joined to accountable intervention
non_trigger: A simple case review or direct measure may answer the decision without mining, prediction or simulation.
trigger: Analytics is proposed to diagnose or recommend process changes.

bearer: AI-generated process artefacts and their independent acceptance checks
criterion: Accepted content is checked against the task’s evidence and intended semantics; uncertainty and unsupported additions remain identifiable.
name: Independently checked AI-assisted modelling
non_trigger: Human modelling, a short narrative or a decision table may be cheaper and more reliable for small or sensitive tasks.
trigger: A generative model is used to elicit, draft, explain or revise a process representation.

bearer: Unresolved autonomous organisational process self-revision capability
criterion: No general operational postcondition is certified. A later bounded system would need demonstrable constraint-respecting action and verified consequences.
name: Autonomous agentic process self-revision
non_trigger: Use bounded assistance, recommendations or explicitly delegated reversible operations while retaining authorised review of consequential redesign.
trigger: An agent is proposed to choose and execute consequential process changes without case-by-case human approval.

bearer: Knowledge-work support, discretion, variants and binding constraints
criterion: A later assessment does not penalise justified discretion merely for departing from the nominal path.
