name: Effective capability and permission checks
non_trigger: A conventional access-control and capability check may suffice; no specialised agent registry is required.
trigger: A role or agent may be allocated work it cannot or may no longer perform.

bearer: A stakeholder/requirements judgement and the actors, dependencies or acceptance statements it concerns: Security-constraint and threat-to-test traceability.
criterion: A security requirement has an operational control and evidence or an explicitly unresolved gap.
name: Security-constraint and threat-to-test traceability
non_trigger: Conventional threat modelling and access-control tests may be sufficient.
trigger: The system handles protected resources, data or adversarial interactions.

bearer: A stakeholder/requirements judgement and the actors, dependencies or acceptance statements it concerns: Non-functional constraints and adverse consequences.
criterion: A successful task is accepted only under the applicable consequence and quality constraints, with unresolved trade-offs exposed.
name: Non-functional constraints and adverse consequences
non_trigger: A narrow low-risk computation can use a small explicit quality budget rather than a full assurance programme.
trigger: Task achievement can cause material cost or harm, or service qualities determine acceptability.

bearer: A stakeholder/requirements judgement and the actors, dependencies or acceptance statements it concerns: Modular requirements views and explicit interfaces.
criterion: Users can reason locally without losing consequential inter-view dependencies.
name: Modular requirements views and explicit interfaces
non_trigger: Keep one small model when splitting would only add navigation and synchronisation costs.
trigger: A full actor/goal diagram becomes difficult for its users to understand or maintain.

bearer: A stakeholder/requirements judgement and the actors, dependencies or acceptance statements it concerns: A complete goal diagram proves complete requirements.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): A complete goal diagram proves complete requirements.
name: A complete goal diagram proves complete requirements
non_trigger: Ask an omitted-actor or false-success question before adding any diagram.
trigger: A model is offered as sufficient acceptance evidence.

bearer: An abstraction or configuration choice among agent and non-agent realisations: Agent-paradigm suitability decision.
criterion: The chosen agent boundary has a stated advantage or necessity, or the non-agent alternative is selected.
name: Agent-paradigm suitability decision
non_trigger: Use objects, services, actors, a workflow or a central controller when they satisfy the needs more simply.
trigger: An agent abstraction or extra autonomous participant is proposed.

bearer: An abstraction or configuration choice among agent and non-agent realisations: Agent-oriented analysis without mandatory agent runtime.
criterion: Stakeholder concepts remain traceable in a conventional implementation without invented agent processes.
name: Agent-oriented analysis without mandatory agent runtime
non_trigger: A conventional requirements method may suffice if it captures the same dependency and responsibility distinctions.
trigger: Social requirements are useful but runtime autonomy is unnecessary or unsuitable.

bearer: An abstraction or configuration choice among agent and non-agent realisations: Explicit autonomy and refusal boundaries.
criterion: Tests show both permitted discretion and refusal/escalation on out-of-scope requests.
name: Explicit autonomy and refusal boundaries
non_trigger: Deterministic constrained execution is sufficient when discretion contributes no value.
trigger: A component selects actions rather than merely executing an already approved sequence.

bearer: An abstraction or configuration choice among agent and non-agent realisations: Every active component should be an agent.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Every active component should be an agent.
name: Every active component should be an agent
non_trigger: Reject the prescription; ordinary components remain legitimate.
trigger: Universal prescription, including simple deterministic modules.

bearer: An abstraction or configuration choice among agent and non-agent realisations: More autonomy is inherently beneficial.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): More autonomy is inherently beneficial.
name: More autonomy is inherently beneficial
non_trigger: Reject; choose bounded discretion or central control where coordination and predictability dominate.
trigger: Universal monotonic benefit claim.

bearer: An abstraction or configuration choice among agent and non-agent realisations: Single-agent and workflow substitution tests.
criterion: An extra participant has attributable value or is removed; null/adverse outcomes are retained.
name: Single-agent and workflow substitution tests
non_trigger: Omit multi-agent execution when the simpler baseline meets the same needs.
trigger: A multi-agent design is being justified on quality, robustness or cost.

bearer: An abstraction or configuration choice among agent and non-agent realisations: Increasing agent count necessarily improves results.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Increasing agent count necessarily improves results.
name: Increasing agent count necessarily improves results
non_trigger: One component, one agent or a workflow remains a legitimate outcome.
trigger: Agent count or conversational diversity is presented as an improvement by itself.

bearer: An abstraction or configuration choice among agent and non-agent realisations: Mental-state labels establish intelligence.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Mental-state labels establish intelligence.
name: Mental-state labels establish intelligence
non_trigger: Terminology can remain useful as a modelling convention without any anthropomorphic inference.
trigger: Mental-state terminology is offered as sufficient evidence of competence.

bearer: An organisational arrangement, role binding or social/normative constraint: Role responsibilities, permissions, activities and protocols.
criterion: Each role obligation has a plausible implementation, interaction and authority basis.
name: Role responsibilities, permissions, activities and protocols
non_trigger: A small interface/responsibility record can carry the same semantics without the Gaia notation.
trigger: Recurring organisational responsibilities need explicit engineering interpretation.

bearer: An organisational arrangement, role binding or social/normative constraint: Many-to-many role-to-agent allocation.
criterion: Responsibilities are neither lost nor accidentally duplicated by implementation cardinality.
name: Many-to-many role-to-agent allocation
non_trigger: A one-to-one mapping is acceptable when justified; no replication is required.
trigger: One agent fulfils several roles or several agents may fulfil one role.

bearer: An organisational arrangement, role binding or social/normative constraint: Organisation-level rules supplement local role contracts.
criterion: A locally permitted assignment can be refused when it violates a collective constraint.
name: Organisation-level rules supplement local role contracts
non_trigger: An ordinary shared invariant or configuration rule can replace a separate organisation model.
trigger: Local correctness permits an invalid collective organisation.

bearer: An organisational arrangement, role binding or social/normative constraint: Collective safety and liveness obligations.
criterion: Evidence addresses the stated global invariant or progress condition under declared assumptions.
name: Collective safety and liveness obligations
non_trigger: A central invariant or simpler serial execution may discharge the obligation more cheaply.
trigger: Correct local agents do not by themselves establish a required system-level property.

bearer: An organisational arrangement, role binding or social/normative constraint: Capability-constrained dynamic organisation.
criterion: A proposed admission, departure or reassignment satisfies the stated goal/capability/organisation constraints; any live-obligation consequences must also satisfy the separate transition criterion.
name: Capability-constrained dynamic organisation
non_trigger: Keep a stable organisation when changes are rare and a controlled redeployment is cheaper.
trigger: Membership, resources or responsibilities change at runtime.

bearer: An organisational arrangement, role binding or social/normative constraint: Explicit dynamic role binding.
criterion: Each message/commitment is attributable to the role holder valid for that instance and time.
name: Explicit dynamic role binding
non_trigger: Static named participants are sufficient in a genuinely closed stable system.
trigger: Open protocols admit participants dynamically or continue across replacements.

bearer: An organisational arrangement, role binding or social/normative constraint: Holonic decomposition.
criterion: Cross-level responsibilities remain explicit rather than hidden by nesting.
name: Holonic decomposition
non_trigger: Flat roles, modules or services are sufficient when hierarchy adds no useful boundary.
trigger: Recursive organisational units genuinely simplify a system's structure or scaling problem.

bearer: An organisational arrangement, role binding or social/normative constraint: Local cooperation as adaptive-system design principle.
criterion: Local repairs are realised and collective effects tested rather than assumed from the label cooperative.
name: Local cooperation as adaptive-system design principle
non_trigger: Stable organisation, explicit allocation or central optimisation may be simpler or more predictable.
trigger: The task admits local cooperation-driven organisation and can tolerate the specified adaptation dynamics.

bearer: An organisational arrangement, role binding or social/normative constraint: Local cooperation as a certificate of global adequacy.
criterion: Does local cooperative adequacy constitute a general certificate of the required external system function, beyond the exact existence/equivalence theorem and stated assumptions?
name: Local cooperation as a certificate of global adequacy
non_trigger: Do not accept the certificate without a suitable theorem and validated premises or adequate collective evidence.
trigger: A local-cooperation method is extended into a universal global guarantee.

bearer: An organisational arrangement, role binding or social/normative constraint: Norm specification, violation and recovery.
criterion: The applicable norm, responsible subject and fulfilment or violation outcome can be established for a concrete interaction, including unresolved evidence.
name: Norm specification, violation and recovery
non_trigger: A hard access rule or a simple externally enforced contract may need no autonomous normative reasoning. A conventional policy table can suffice.
trigger: Open organisations or applications with consequential social obligations, sanctions or rules whose violation must remain visible.

bearer: An organisational arrangement, role binding or social/normative constraint: Negotiation and task-allocation procedure.
criterion: The awarded task, responsible performer, accepted terms and actual result can be distinguished and checked.
name: Negotiation and task-allocation procedure
non_trigger: Static assignment or a central scheduler is preferable when information and authority are centralised and negotiation adds no benefit.
trigger: Work or resources must be allocated among independently capable participants with locally held information.

bearer: An organisational arrangement, role binding or social/normative constraint: Agent, organisation and environment separation.
criterion: An organisational or resource change has identifiable effects on agent behaviour rather than silently changing several meanings at once.
name: Agent, organisation and environment separation
non_trigger: A small cohesive programme may keep these concerns together when the distinctions remain clear and modular separation adds no value.
trigger: Systems where roles, norms, resource operations and individual plans evolve independently.

bearer: An organisational arrangement, role binding or social/normative constraint: Static cooperative organisation as a universal premise.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Static cooperative organisation as a universal premise.
name: Static cooperative organisation as a universal premise
non_trigger: Keep the original simpler branch when its assumptions are actually stable.
trigger: An original closed-world method is transferred to dynamic, open or competing participants.

bearer: A public interaction, protocol enactment or communication interpretation: Interaction contract with defined semantics.
criterion: Exchanged messages and actions can be checked against the specified interaction, including unexpected paths.
name: Interaction contract with defined semantics
non_trigger: A simple typed API with explicit pre/postconditions may suffice.
trigger: Multiple independently implemented participants must interoperate or coordinate.

bearer: A public interaction, protocol enactment or communication interpretation: Content and ontology alignment.
criterion: The same exchanged values denote compatible entities and constraints at both ends.
name: Content and ontology alignment
non_trigger: An agreed small schema and worked examples may replace a large ontology.
trigger: Heterogeneous agents exchange content whose meanings can differ.

bearer: A public interaction, protocol enactment or communication interpretation: Observable social commitments.
criterion: Participants can assess whether the defined commitment holds, is discharged or is violated.
name: Observable social commitments
non_trigger: A conventional contract/state record may be adequate where its semantics and lifecycle are clear.
trigger: Independent parties need assessable obligations without exposing or trusting each other's private mental state.

bearer: A public interaction, protocol enactment or communication interpretation: Private mental-state semantics as open compliance criterion.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Private mental-state semantics as open compliance criterion.
name: Private mental-state semantics as open compliance criterion
non_trigger: Reject as a general public compliance criterion; use observable contractual/protocol conditions.
trigger: Open heterogeneous interaction where others cannot inspect mental states.

bearer: A public interaction, protocol enactment or communication interpretation: Private mental states as the basis of communication compliance.
criterion: Under what private-state access, cooperation and semantic assumptions is mental-state communication semantics a useful engineering constraint, without being a general open-system public-compliance certificate?
name: Private mental states as the basis of communication compliance
non_trigger: Use public commitments or operational interface conditions for heterogeneous open participants.
trigger: The claimed meaning of a message depends on beliefs or intentions attributed to its sender.

bearer: A public interaction, protocol enactment or communication interpretation: Local protocol conformance and information causality.
criterion: Local traces obey the relevant dependencies; unresolved global or external-effect claims remain separate.
name: Local protocol conformance and information causality
non_trigger: Direct shared-state or ordinary request-response implementation can suffice if its semantics discharge the same obligations.
trigger: Protocol participants act asynchronously or use different implementation platforms.

bearer: A public interaction, protocol enactment or communication interpretation: Fault, timeout and compensation semantics.
criterion: A failure ends in a known safe/accepted state, a transferred obligation or explicitly unresolved status.
name: Fault, timeout and compensation semantics
non_trigger: A fail-fast result is sufficient when no external partial effect or live obligation remains.
trigger: Actions or interactions may fail, partially succeed or remain unobserved.

bearer: A public interaction, protocol enactment or communication interpretation: Protocol evolution and mixed-version compatibility.
criterion: Mixed versions either interoperate within declared rules or fail/transition explicitly.
name: Protocol evolution and mixed-version compatibility
non_trigger: Stop, drain and redeploy a small closed system when live migration adds unnecessary risk.
trigger: A protocol/schema changes without stopping every participant and obligation.

bearer: A public interaction, protocol enactment or communication interpretation: Interaction identity and authentication.
criterion: A consequential request has a verifiable origin and action-specific authority or is treated as untrusted.
name: Interaction identity and authentication
non_trigger: A genuinely closed trusted execution boundary may use ordinary process identity; do not impose public-key infrastructure without a relevant threat.
trigger: Heterogeneous, open or remote interactions in which impersonation or mistaken attribution matters.

bearer: A public interaction, protocol enactment or communication interpretation: Communication uncertainty, correlation and delivery handling.
criterion: An observed conversation can be matched to its participants and protocol instance, with missing, duplicate or out-of-order events handled explicitly.
name: Communication uncertainty, correlation and delivery handling
non_trigger: Reliable in-process calls can use ordinary call semantics if the actual boundary satisfies those assumptions.
trigger: Asynchronous or failure-prone communication and heterogeneous implementations.

bearer: A public interaction, protocol enactment or communication interpretation: ACL syntax guarantees semantic interoperability.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): ACL syntax guarantees semantic interoperability.
name: ACL syntax guarantees semantic interoperability
non_trigger: A simpler shared API contract can establish the necessary agreement without adopting ACL machinery.
trigger: Heterogeneous agents exchange well-formed messages and are assumed to understand and comply with one another.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Explicit environment and effect interfaces.
criterion: The engineer can distinguish stale belief, attempted action and observed external change.
name: Explicit environment and effect interfaces
non_trigger: A narrow input/output contract is sufficient for an isolated deterministic computation.
trigger: The system interacts with an independently changing software or physical environment.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Engineered environment artefacts.
criterion: The state and effects of a shared resource can be inspected independently of any one agent's narrative.
name: Engineered environment artefacts
non_trigger: Ordinary service interfaces, data structures or databases are adequate when they expose the necessary state and operations.
trigger: Several agents interact through persistent resources, tools or coordination artefacts.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Problem-matched internal architecture, including guarded BDI design.
criterion: Internal concepts have an implementation interpretation rather than merely anthropomorphic labels.
name: Problem-matched internal architecture, including guarded BDI design
non_trigger: A direct state machine or ordinary behaviour implementation may be sufficient.
trigger: An agent’s internal decision mechanism is being designed.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Explicit plan failure and goal persistence semantics.
criterion: Tests distinguish plan failure, alternative-plan selection, goal success and authorised abandonment.
name: Explicit plan failure and goal persistence semantics
non_trigger: A single explicit error return is enough for a one-shot operation with no continuing goal.
trigger: An agent has alternative means or long-lived goals under uncertain action outcomes.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Goal completion checked against consequences.
criterion: Goal lifecycle transitions reflect the declared success condition, not merely exhausted steps.
name: Goal completion checked against consequences
non_trigger: An ordinary postcondition check is sufficient for a deterministic local goal.
trigger: An internal goal is declared achieved after an action or conversation.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Capability and plan modularity.
criterion: Changes within a module do not silently alter unrelated goal selection or failure behaviour.
name: Capability and plan modularity
non_trigger: A small readable plan library may need no extra module layer.
trigger: Large BDI code bases or reused capabilities have hidden coupling.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Belief provenance, revision and observational uncertainty.
criterion: A consequential belief can be traced to an inspected observation or derivation and revised or withheld when its support fails.
name: Belief provenance, revision and observational uncertainty
non_trigger: A deterministic local computation over immutable, validated input may require only ordinary input checks rather than a belief-provenance subsystem.
trigger: Agents whose observations become stale, conflict or are derived from fallible models.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Intention retention and bounded reconsideration.
criterion: The system can explain why pursuit continued, was suspended or was abandoned, and what happened to dependent obligations.
name: Intention retention and bounded reconsideration
non_trigger: A one-shot deterministic operation may need no persistent intention state; a standard job lifecycle can implement the necessary persistence.
trigger: Long-lived, interruptible or resource-bounded goal pursuit where continual replanning or blind persistence causes harm.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Authorised goal adoption, maintenance and abandonment.
criterion: Each active goal has a legitimate origin and explicit lifecycle state, with satisfaction or abandonment justified by the appropriate evidence.
name: Authorised goal adoption, maintenance and abandonment
non_trigger: For one fixed authorised objective, an ordinary precondition, task and postcondition may be adequate.
trigger: Multiple goal sources, maintenance requirements, delegated tasks or behaviour that persists after a request changes.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Reactive–deliberative arbitration.
criterion: A triggered urgent event is handled within the declared scope, with the interrupted task and effects accounted for.
name: Reactive–deliberative arbitration
non_trigger: A purely reactive controller or a sequential job processor may dominate where goals do not require deliberative persistence.
trigger: Urgent events can arrive during planning or multiple behaviours compete for shared resources.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Interference among concurrent intentions.
criterion: An individually valid plan cannot silently invalidate another plan’s relied-on preconditions.
name: Interference among concurrent intentions
non_trigger: Serialise a small critical region when this preserves required responsiveness.
trigger: Plans overlap in time or manipulate shared state.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Uncertainty-aware decision and abstention policy.
criterion: The decision records what uncertainty mattered and why action or abstention met the applicable criterion.
name: Uncertainty-aware decision and abstention policy
non_trigger: Deterministic validated inputs and reversible low-consequence actions may justify a simpler direct policy.
trigger: Partial observations, uncertain consequences, stochastic components or material model/environment mismatch.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Explicit temporal feasibility for goals, plans and actions.
criterion: Claimed deadlines specify excluded costs and the operating assumptions under which evidence applies.
name: Explicit temporal feasibility for goals, plans and actions
non_trigger: Ordinary timeout or measured service-level tests suffice for soft deadlines; avoid hard-real-time claims without their prerequisites.
trigger: Timeliness is part of success or safety, not merely a performance preference.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Resource budgets and termination conditions.
criterion: Termination has a recorded reason and reconciles unresolved work rather than confusing stopped execution with achieved goals.
name: Resource budgets and termination conditions
non_trigger: A statically bounded operation may need only ordinary timeout and cost limits.
trigger: Autonomous or conversational loops can continue indefinitely or consume unacceptable resources.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Design-to-implementation correspondence.
criterion: A design obligation has an identified implementation realisation and evidence of relevant behaviour.
name: Design-to-implementation correspondence
non_trigger: A small reviewed mapping plus targeted tests may be sufficient for a simple implementation.
trigger: Implementation, generation or migration changes the representation of the design.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Qualified model transformation trust.
criterion: Generated output satisfies the stated mapped obligations or exposes unsupported semantics.
name: Qualified model transformation trust
non_trigger: Manual implementation with explicit correspondence may be cheaper for small or rapidly changing models.
trigger: Code or executable artefacts are generated from a model.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Explicit manual and platform obligations.
criterion: No relevant obligation is credited merely because a framework exists or an artefact was generated.
name: Explicit manual and platform obligations
non_trigger: A concise responsibility/feature-boundary note is enough; no exhaustive checklist if the missing obligations are clear.
trigger: A method or framework is selected, especially with generators or abstractions that hide work.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Cross-view and metamodel consistency checking.
criterion: A checked consistency claim states the views, versions, mapping and scope; detected conflicts have a responsible decision-maker.
name: Cross-view and metamodel consistency checking
non_trigger: One unambiguous representation with executable tests may need no separate cross-view checker.
trigger: Multiple views or generated artefacts describe overlapping behaviours and inconsistent assumptions could survive local review.

bearer: An agent design, internal decision process, environment interface or executable realisation: Knowledge and task modelling as distinct engineering views.
criterion: Reusable inference patterns have an explicit task and domain interpretation.
name: Knowledge and task modelling as distinct engineering views
non_trigger: A direct typed representation and small algorithm are enough for simple reasoning.
trigger: Knowledge-intensive reasoning is difficult to engineer as undifferentiated code or beliefs.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: Lifecycle scope and method suitability.
criterion: Requirements, construction, assurance and operation have an explicit coverage argument with justified omissions.
name: Lifecycle scope and method suitability
non_trigger: A smaller situational method is sufficient when it addresses all relevant obligations with less overhead.
trigger: A named methodology is considered for a concrete engineering endeavour.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: Semantic compatibility of method fragments.
criterion: A fragment's output actually supplies the assumptions its successor or concurrent consumer needs.
name: Semantic compatibility of method fragments
non_trigger: One coherent existing method may be cheaper than a tailored hybrid.
trigger: Elements of different methods are combined or replaced.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: Work-product prerequisites and consistency.
criterion: An activity does not consume an obsolete or semantically incompatible prerequisite unnoticed.
name: Work-product prerequisites and consistency
non_trigger: A short dependency note or shared working representation may suffice.
trigger: Several engineering activities depend on evolving models or decisions.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: Executable prescriptions and work-product consumers.
criterion: Practitioners can execute the prescription and recognise its relevant result.
name: Executable prescriptions and work-product consumers
non_trigger: A direct decision rule or established team practice is enough if it supplies the needed result.
trigger: A method claims to support an engineering concern.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: Consumer-directed cross-view and operational feedback.
criterion: A counterexample can reach the model or requirement that made it possible.
name: Consumer-directed cross-view and operational feedback
non_trigger: A small stable task may complete in one pass; no artificial iteration count is required.
trigger: Later work reveals missing constraints or invalid assumptions.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: Proportionate admission, assembly and retirement of method machinery.
criterion: Every retained task has a live function and every removed task leaves no unaddressed relied-on obligation.
name: Proportionate admission, assembly and retirement of method machinery
non_trigger: Omit unused machinery; retain a smaller evidence or coordination mechanism when adequate.
trigger: A method is tailored, becomes costly or contains work with no current decision use.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: Comparison beyond feature checklists.
criterion: Selection reasons remain defensible when feature counts are replaced by observed utility and cost.
name: Comparison beyond feature checklists
non_trigger: A bounded pilot on the actual task may be more informative than an encyclopaedic comparison matrix.
trigger: A method is selected, taught, purchased or claimed superior.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: Learnability and modelling burden.
criterion: Users can perform the consequential modelling/review/change task, not merely recognise notation.
name: Learnability and modelling burden
non_trigger: A simpler representation or training-limited subset may be adequate.
trigger: Expressive notation, large models or specialised tools are introduced.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: Scoped reuse of engineering assets.
criterion: The reused asset's assumptions and adaptations are documented to the degree required by its actual consumers.
name: Scoped reuse of engineering assets
non_trigger: A one-off simple solution may cost less than discovering, adapting and governing a reusable asset.
trigger: Repeated engineering problems with a genuinely shared structure or stable platform.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: Method revision under declared authority.
criterion: Revisions state what changed, why, what evidence applies and which continuity obligations remain.
name: Method revision under declared authority
non_trigger: Minor editorial changes need only consistency checking; do not manufacture a meta-process for every edit.
trigger: Method fragments, acceptance rules or modelling conventions are revised.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: One mandatory serial lifecycle.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): One mandatory serial lifecycle.
name: One mandatory serial lifecycle
non_trigger: Reject as a general requirement; use actual prerequisite relations and iterations.
trigger: Universal sequencing rule independent of dependencies and feedback.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: Union of all methods as a superior method.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Union of all methods as a superior method.
name: Union of all methods as a superior method
non_trigger: Reject; select a compatible subset with explicit interfaces and omissions.
trigger: Unconditional union of alternative schools and fragments.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: Method quality equals named-phase or diagram count.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Method quality equals named-phase or diagram count.
name: Method quality equals named-phase or diagram count
non_trigger: Test one consequential engineering task against the proposed method.
trigger: A methodology comparison rewards labels rather than operative support.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: Named-method observance as assurance.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Named-method observance as assurance.
name: Named-method observance as assurance
non_trigger: Inspect the consequential mechanism directly and accept an adequate unnamed equivalent.
trigger: Method compliance is used to close an unresolved engineering question.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: Universally exhaustive methodology artefacts.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Universally exhaustive methodology artefacts.
name: Universally exhaustive methodology artefacts
non_trigger: A short shared record, executable specification or direct observation can replace a larger ritual where it meets the same need.
trigger: Compliance is judged by artefact presence irrespective of decision use or risk.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: One mandatory methodology fits every agent system.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): One mandatory methodology fits every agent system.
name: One mandatory methodology fits every agent system
non_trigger: Use a small conventional method or a tailored AOSE configuration where sufficient.
trigger: A branded process is proposed unchanged across incompatible kinds of agency, organisation and assurance.

bearer: An engineering method configuration, fragment, decision procedure or associated method claim: A consistent fragment composition guarantees achievable goals.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): A consistent fragment composition guarantees achievable goals.
name: A consistent fragment composition guarantees achievable goals
non_trigger: Use a small feasibility or counterexample check on the actual combined obligations.
trigger: Semantic method integration is presented as automatic system-level adequacy.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Requirements-to-behaviour traceability.
criterion: A changed requirement identifies potentially affected behaviour/evidence and unexplained gaps.
name: Requirements-to-behaviour traceability
non_trigger: A compact requirement-to-test mapping may replace a traceability tool or exhaustive graph.
trigger: Changes or acceptance decisions require knowing which implemented behaviour supports which concern.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Bounded programme model checking.
criterion: The named property holds or a counterexample is found within the stated model and bounds.
name: Bounded programme model checking
non_trigger: Testing, static checks or simpler deterministic design may be more proportionate.
trigger: A consequential finite/bounded behaviour space or suitable abstraction can be formally analysed.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Explicit model and environment assumptions for formal assurance.
criterion: A proof over a finite or abstract model is not presented as a theorem about unrestricted deployment.
name: Explicit model and environment assumptions for formal assurance
non_trigger: Use bounded tests instead when formalisation costs exceed its decision value, while retaining uncertainty.
trigger: A proof or model-checking result supports acceptance.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Operating-environment and abstraction validity.
criterion: The environmental abstraction and test context are justified for the claimed operating setting, with unestablished conditions named.
name: Operating-environment and abstraction validity
non_trigger: A direct representative effect test may suffice for a narrow well-observed environment.
trigger: Formal, simulation or benchmark evidence is used to support real operation.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Validated percept–belief and action–effect mappings.
criterion: A correct internal belief update or action request is not mistaken for a correct measurement or achieved effect.
name: Validated percept–belief and action–effect mappings
non_trigger: Direct boundary tests and observable effect checks may suffice.
trigger: Correct decisions depend on sensors, tools, actuators or state-estimation assumptions.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Assure both individual behaviour and collective outcomes.
criterion: Locally passing agents are not assumed to establish a correct system.
name: Assure both individual behaviour and collective outcomes
non_trigger: For one non-interacting component, collective assurance is not a separate activity.
trigger: Several agents or services jointly realise a requirement.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Explicit compositional assurance assumptions.
criterion: Each claimed system guarantee identifies its local warrants and environmental assumptions, including any obligation not established.
name: Explicit compositional assurance assumptions
non_trigger: Direct system-level tests and a small architecture may be cheaper than a formal assume–guarantee calculus, while still requiring explicit critical assumptions.
trigger: Local analyses or independent components are combined into a consequential system.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Agent-level test oracles.
criterion: Tests discriminate relevant failures including apparently successful but prohibited behaviour.
name: Agent-level test oracles
non_trigger: Simple deterministic assertions are sufficient when they capture the actual success and harm conditions.
trigger: Agent output or behaviour needs a pass/fail or acceptance decision.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Adversarial integration and discriminating perturbation testing.
criterion: Specified fault/interleaving cases produce acceptable outcomes or clearly exposed failures.
name: Adversarial integration and discriminating perturbation testing
non_trigger: A conventional integration test may suffice; no adversarial MAS simulation is needed without a relevant threat.
trigger: Several agents/environment components jointly realise an obligation or share a hazard.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Risk-proportionate test adequacy.
criterion: Reported coverage names its denominator and omissions; adverse cases can change the criterion.
name: Risk-proportionate test adequacy
non_trigger: Use cheaper edge, condition, scenario, property-based or risk-focused criteria when they address the claim.
trigger: Agent branching and recovery create many possible behaviours.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Simulation validity and transfer limits.
criterion: Claims remain conditional on calibrated features and do not silently become production success rates.
name: Simulation validity and transfer limits
non_trigger: Use a direct small deployment trial when it is safe and more informative; simulation may be unnecessary.
trigger: Simulated performance or agent-based modelling informs implementation or operational decisions.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Explanation fidelity and human interpretation.
criterion: Explanation claims correspond to logged/modelled events and help the relevant user task under evaluation.
name: Explanation fidelity and human interpretation
non_trigger: A clear state/error message or direct evidence may suffice; a narrative is not always needed.
trigger: A user, designer or operator needs to understand a consequential decision or debug behaviour.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: All-path testing as the only adequate assurance.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): All-path testing as the only adequate assurance.
name: All-path testing as the only adequate assurance
non_trigger: Superseded by declared risk- and property-sensitive adequacy in 047, with proofs and other testing where appropriate.
trigger: Universal adequacy rule derived from the size of goal-plan execution spaces.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Exhaustive testing guarantees unrestricted autonomous behaviour.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Exhaustive testing guarantees unrestricted autonomous behaviour.
name: Exhaustive testing guarantees unrestricted autonomous behaviour
non_trigger: A finite exhaustive test remains valid for its actually finite, enumerated model.
trigger: A demonstration or finite test suite is used to guarantee every autonomous response.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Code generation as an assurance certificate.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Code generation as an assurance certificate.
name: Code generation as an assurance certificate
non_trigger: Reject; require model validation, qualified transformation and implementation/environment evidence.
trigger: A generator produces executable code from a model.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Complete models guarantee correct implementation.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Complete models guarantee correct implementation.
name: Complete models guarantee correct implementation
non_trigger: A smaller adequate model with tested implementation may be sufficient.
trigger: A complete set of diagrams or generated artefacts is used as a delivery certificate.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Model checking certifies the deployed system without correspondence evidence.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Model checking certifies the deployed system without correspondence evidence.
name: Model checking certifies the deployed system without correspondence evidence
non_trigger: Model checking can be valuable for a bounded claim without a universal certificate.
trigger: A proof about an abstract agent programme is offered as assurance of all deployed behaviour.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Agent agreement as an independent correctness oracle.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Agent agreement as an independent correctness oracle.
name: Agent agreement as an independent correctness oracle
non_trigger: Reject as a general oracle; use external evidence or genuinely independent validated checks.
trigger: Several agents or role prompts endorse the same answer or action.

bearer: An assurance claim and its specified object, oracle, model or implementation evidence: Independent action-effect verification.
criterion: Attempt, execution acknowledgement, observed effect and accepted outcome are not silently substituted.
name: Independent action-effect verification
non_trigger: Direct return-value checking suffices only when that return reliably establishes the relevant effect.
trigger: An agent claims to have changed an external object or discharged an obligation.

bearer: An operational system state, transition, change or evidence handoff: Runtime conformance monitoring.
criterion: A detected relevant violation changes a decision, action or explicitly accepted risk.
name: Runtime conformance monitoring
non_trigger: Periodic inspection or an existing infrastructure monitor may suffice for slowly changing low-risk behaviour.
trigger: Long-lived, adaptive or open operation may depart from design assumptions.

bearer: An operational system state, transition, change or evidence handoff: Operational trace correlation.
criterion: An observed effect can be related to its request/attempt and relevant configuration or labelled uncorrelated.
name: Operational trace correlation
non_trigger: A single ordered trace is enough for one process; do not build distributed tracing without need.
trigger: Failures, assurance or accountability require tracing distributed execution.

bearer: An operational system state, transition, change or evidence handoff: Trace-grounded multi-agent failure localisation.
criterion: The diagnosis points to a testable defect hypothesis and avoids blaming every failure on the model or coordination.
name: Trace-grounded multi-agent failure localisation
non_trigger: A simple error report suffices when the fault is already isolated.
trigger: A multi-agent run fails and diagnosis can change a repair or evaluation.

bearer: An operational system state, transition, change or evidence handoff: Versioned reproducible deployment configuration.
criterion: A reported behaviour/evaluation can be tied to a sufficiently specified deployed configuration.
name: Versioned reproducible deployment configuration
non_trigger: A small versioned configuration and test environment record may suffice.
trigger: A result or live system depends on mutable implementation/configuration components.

bearer: An operational system state, transition, change or evidence handoff: Selective premise-sensitive revalidation of assurance and requirements.
criterion: A material change causes affected support/applicability and acceptance obligations to be re-examined at the appropriate scope. Changed assumptions may invalidate support without logically falsifying the conclusion; unaffected evidence is not discarded indiscriminately.
name: Selective premise-sensitive revalidation of assurance and requirements
non_trigger: No revalidation is needed for a proved irrelevant change; a targeted regression may suffice.
trigger: Requirements, semantics, implementation, permissions, membership, model or environment assumptions change.

bearer: An operational system state, transition, change or evidence handoff: Authorised adaptation boundaries.
criterion: A revision stays within authority and its changed assumptions/effects are evaluated.
name: Authorised adaptation boundaries
non_trigger: Manual authorised redeployment is sufficient where automation adds little value.
trigger: A system can reorganise, learn, replace plans/policies or change its own operation.

bearer: An operational system state, transition, change or evidence handoff: Valid continuity or resolution of obligations across operational transitions.
criterion: A structurally valid new organisation does not erase the commitments created by its predecessor configuration.
name: Valid continuity or resolution of obligations across operational transitions
non_trigger: Drain in-flight work before reconfiguration, or retain a static assignment when continuity cannot be established.
trigger: An adaptive organisation changes role holders while interactions or commitments remain live.

bearer: An operational system state, transition, change or evidence handoff: Consequential evidence reaches an authorised capable consumer.
criterion: The evidence is usable at the relevant consequential decision, rather than merely stored or addressed to a nominal owner.
name: Consequential evidence reaches an authorised capable consumer
non_trigger: A direct conversation plus maintained configuration may be adequate in a small team.
trigger: Work crosses development, testing, operation or affected-user boundaries.

bearer: An operational system state, transition, change or evidence handoff: Deployment and legacy-integration obligations.
criterion: The deployment has responsible operators and tested integration boundaries rather than only runnable agent code.
name: Deployment and legacy-integration obligations
non_trigger: Reuse an established deployment process and explicit interface contract where adequate.
trigger: An agent application enters an existing operational environment.

bearer: An operational system state, transition, change or evidence handoff: Deployment topology and trust-boundary design.
criterion: Each consequential interaction has an actual path and trust/failure boundary consistent with its specified semantics.
name: Deployment topology and trust-boundary design
non_trigger: A single process or conventional service can be the correct deployment for several conceptual roles.
trigger: Distribution changes what can fail, who controls state or which guarantees interactions can rely on.

bearer: An operational system state, transition, change or evidence handoff: Idempotency and uncertain-effect reconciliation.
criterion: A retry cannot silently produce an unrecognised duplicate consequence; uncertain outcomes remain explicit until reconciled.
name: Idempotency and uncertain-effect reconciliation
non_trigger: A pure computation or an atomic in-process operation with no surviving external effect may need no extra deduplication mechanism.
trigger: Tool calls or distributed actions can outlive a timeout, interruption or process restart.

bearer: An operational system state, transition, change or evidence handoff: Human participation and effective intervention.
criterion: A human decision reaches the execution boundary and its effect or inability to halt an action is observable.
name: Human participation and effective intervention
non_trigger: Low-risk, fully specified reversible operations may not need human approval at every step; prior policy can be sufficient.
trigger: High-consequence delegation, contested requirements or operational exceptions outside authorised autonomy.

bearer: An operational system state, transition, change or evidence handoff: Accountability and evidence custody.
criterion: A relevant action can be attributed and its supporting evidence inspected or explicitly reported unavailable without silent alteration.
name: Accountability and evidence custody
non_trigger: Ephemeral low-risk calculations may need only ordinary diagnostic information; do not log everything by default.
trigger: Disputed obligations, externally consequential actions or failures requiring explanation and remedy.

bearer: An operational system state, transition, change or evidence handoff: Design-method support implies a complete operational lifecycle.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Design-method support implies a complete operational lifecycle.
name: Design-method support implies a complete operational lifecycle
non_trigger: Supplement it with existing operational practices and label the documented import.
trigger: A method is represented as complete because it reaches implementation.

bearer: An operational system state, transition, change or evidence handoff: Unmonitored self-modification as authorised evolution.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Unmonitored self-modification as authorised evolution.
name: Unmonitored self-modification as authorised evolution
non_trigger: Reject; use authorised bounded adaptation and independent acceptance conditions.
trigger: Runtime plan, policy, prompt or permission changes are possible.

bearer: An operational system state, transition, change or evidence handoff: Observation plus self-revision guarantees improvement.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Observation plus self-revision guarantees improvement.
name: Observation plus self-revision guarantees improvement
non_trigger: Use bounded reviewed changes and a stable acceptance comparison; leave unresolved trade-offs explicit.
trigger: A feedback loop is treated as self-authorising evidence of maturity or eventual correctness.

bearer: A comparative engineering/evidence claim with a declared intervention, comparator and population: Distinguish model, demonstration, prototype and deployment.
criterion: An industrially authored simulation is not counted as deployment; one flight experiment is not a population frequency.
name: Distinguish model, demonstration, prototype and deployment
non_trigger: A concise evidence label and locator may be sufficient.
trigger: A source is used to justify maturity, adoption or effectiveness.

bearer: A comparative engineering/evidence claim with a declared intervention, comparator and population: Realistic cost-and-quality comparative baselines.
criterion: The claimed advantage is separated from extra computation, tool changes and unfair comparator restrictions.
name: Realistic cost-and-quality comparative baselines
non_trigger: A modest paired pilot or ablation may be enough for a local decision.
trigger: A mechanism or multi-agent design is claimed to improve engineering or outcomes.

bearer: A comparative engineering/evidence claim with a declared intervention, comparator and population: Training, integration and maintenance cost accounting.
criterion: Cost claims state included/excluded work and do not equate fewer glue-code lines with net benefit.
name: Training, integration and maintenance cost accounting
non_trigger: A bounded cost record for the affected phase is enough when the claim is explicitly phase-limited.
trigger: A method is defended on saved coding/modelling time or lower operating burden.

bearer: A comparative engineering/evidence claim with a declared intervention, comparator and population: Comparison-unit and evidence-independence accounting.
criterion: The claimed strength and generality do not count the same experiment, dataset or programme as independent confirmations.
name: Comparison-unit and evidence-independence accounting
non_trigger: A transparent single-case rationale can support a narrow reversible decision without inventing generality.
trigger: Several studies or large reported gains support a general engineering-benefit claim.

bearer: A comparative engineering/evidence claim with a declared intervention, comparator and population: Whole Evolved-AOSE configuration-family net lifecycle benefit.
criterion: Does the newly synthesised conditional Evolved-AOSE configuration family produce greater net lifecycle benefit than the best applicable conventional alternatives under comparable requirements and resources?
name: Whole Evolved-AOSE configuration-family net lifecycle benefit
non_trigger: Use narrower supported mechanism claims and local trials; do not presume system-level superiority.
trigger: Whole-method effectiveness claim spanning tasks and lifecycles.

bearer: A comparative engineering/evidence claim with a declared intervention, comparator and population: Broad whole-AOSE-method superiority over conventional engineering.
criterion: Do complete AOSE methodologies broadly outperform competent conventional engineering across comparable projects and lifecycle outcomes?
name: Broad whole-AOSE-method superiority over conventional engineering
non_trigger: Choose a guarded mechanism on a local business case without claiming whole-method dominance.
trigger: An organisation seeks a general superiority claim rather than a local mechanism or application argument.

bearer: A comparative engineering/evidence claim with a declared intervention, comparator and population: Platform popularity as evidence of method effectiveness.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Platform popularity as evidence of method effectiveness.
name: Platform popularity as evidence of method effectiveness
non_trigger: Reject the inference; examine actual use, scope, costs and results.
trigger: An adoption or maturity claim is inferred from a catalogue or community presence.

bearer: A bounded learned/symbolic agent-engineering component or modern translation: Documented continuity rather than rebranding.
criterion: Historical relations are no stronger than the cited evidence permits.
name: Documented continuity rather than rebranding
non_trigger: Describe mechanisms directly when no ancestry claim is needed.
trigger: A new framework or hybrid is described as AOSE's descendant or replacement.

bearer: A bounded learned/symbolic agent-engineering component or modern translation: LLM role prompts are not role-contract enforcement.
criterion: Role constraints are tested at the relevant action/protocol boundary or explicitly labelled unenforced.
name: LLM role prompts are not role-contract enforcement
non_trigger: Use a prompt as a soft behavioural hint when no enforceable obligation is being claimed.
trigger: LLM participants are assigned roles with permissions, responsibilities or acceptance duties.

bearer: A bounded learned/symbolic agent-engineering component or modern translation: Stochastic and version-sensitive regression evaluation.
criterion: Results state repetitions, variance/uncertainty and version scope rather than a single successful demonstration.
name: Stochastic and version-sensitive regression evaluation
non_trigger: Deterministic checks suffice for deterministic components; local sampling should match the claim and risk.
trigger: Learned/stochastic behaviour or remote updates affect outcomes.

bearer: A bounded learned/symbolic agent-engineering component or modern translation: Tool-use authority separated from generated intention.
criterion: Untrusted or out-of-scope generated intent cannot silently become an authorised action.
name: Tool-use authority separated from generated intention
non_trigger: An ordinary validated API call behind access control is sufficient; no special agent governor is assumed.
trigger: A learned agent can select or construct an effectful operation.

bearer: A bounded learned/symbolic agent-engineering component or modern translation: Untrusted-input and prompt-injection containment.
criterion: Adversarial content does not obtain unauthorised disclosure/action in the tested scope, with residual cases retained.
name: Untrusted-input and prompt-injection containment
non_trigger: No injection-specific machinery is needed for a non-generative parser with a validated narrow grammar and no instruction-following exposure.
trigger: LLM agents consume attacker-influenced content while possessing tools or private data.

bearer: A bounded learned/symbolic agent-engineering component or modern translation: Memory provenance and update semantics.
criterion: A consequential remembered claim can be traced to evidence or labelled uncertain; stale/conflicting entries have a response.
name: Memory provenance and update semantics
non_trigger: Short-lived explicit state may suffice when long-term retrieval adds no value.
trigger: Persistent or shared learned-agent memory influences future decisions.

bearer: A bounded learned/symbolic agent-engineering component or modern translation: Bounded symbolic–learned hybrid design.
criterion: Learned outputs remain bounded inputs to accountable execution and assurance.
name: Bounded symbolic–learned hybrid design
non_trigger: A deterministic or purely symbolic component is preferable when it satisfies the task adequately.
trigger: Language understanding, proposal generation or adaptation helps a system whose obligations cannot be left wholly implicit.

bearer: A bounded learned/symbolic agent-engineering component or modern translation: Generated plans remain subject to executable constraints.
criterion: Plausible natural-language plans are not treated as executable specifications or accepted proofs.
name: Generated plans remain subject to executable constraints
non_trigger: Keep a verified finite plan library or require manual selection when generation offers no justified benefit.
trigger: A planner or learned model generates or revises executable behaviour.

bearer: A bounded learned/symbolic agent-engineering component or modern translation: Preserve responsiveness during long-running plan generation.
criterion: Waiting for a plan does not by itself disable every unrelated reactive obligation; the wait has an explicit failure or resumption path.
name: Preserve responsiveness during long-running plan generation
non_trigger: Use a prewritten plan or synchronous execution when no concurrent response obligation exists and the delay is acceptable.
trigger: Remote or computationally slow plan generation threatens the response time of other responsibilities assigned to the same agent.

bearer: A bounded learned/symbolic agent-engineering component or modern translation: A role prompt is a formal role contract.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): A role prompt is a formal role contract.
name: A role prompt is a formal role contract
non_trigger: Use a small explicit contract and independent permission/test boundary when consequences warrant it.
trigger: Prompt text is offered as sufficient organisational or safety assurance.

bearer: A bounded learned/symbolic agent-engineering component or modern translation: Role prompts alone constitute AOSE.
criterion: Candidate proposition under examination (not endorsed): Role prompts alone constitute AOSE.
name: Role prompts alone constitute AOSE
non_trigger: A useful role prompt may be an adequate local implementation aid without a full methodology claim.
trigger: Modern role-based systems are presented as complete engineering methods solely because their prompts name roles.
